chunks.title: Assessment: Industry Selection
chunks.content:
PQC Assessment Wizard — Step 1: Industry Selection

The Industry Selection step determines which compliance frameworks, threat scenarios, and migration priorities are relevant to your organization. Different industries face varying levels of quantum risk — for example, Financial Services and Government/Defense face the highest urgency due to long-lived data and regulatory mandates.

chunks.title: Assessment: Country Selection
chunks.content:
PQC Assessment Wizard — Step 2: Country Selection

The Country Selection step identifies which national PQC mandates and deadlines apply. Countries like the United States (CNSA 2.0), France (ANSSI), and Germany (BSI) have specific PQC migration timelines. This selection also filters compliance frameworks to show only relevant regulations.

chunks.title: Assessment: Current Cryptographic Usage
chunks.content:
PQC Assessment Wizard — Step 3: Current Cryptographic Usage

The Current Cryptographic Usage step identifies which classical algorithms your organization uses (RSA, ECDSA, ECDH, AES, SHA-2, etc.). This determines which PQC replacements are needed — RSA/ECDSA require ML-DSA or SLH-DSA for signatures, while ECDH requires ML-KEM for key exchange.

chunks.title: Assessment: Data Sensitivity
chunks.content:
PQC Assessment Wizard — Step 4: Data Sensitivity

Data Sensitivity drives urgency assessment. Organizations handling Top Secret, classified, financial, or health data face higher HNDL (Harvest Now, Decrypt Later) risk because adversaries may already be collecting encrypted data for future quantum decryption. Multiple sensitivity levels can be selected — the highest level determines the risk score.

chunks.title: Assessment: Compliance Frameworks
chunks.content:
PQC Assessment Wizard — Step 5: Compliance Frameworks

The Compliance step identifies which regulatory frameworks apply to your organization (CNSA 2.0, NIST guidelines, ANSSI requirements, BSI recommendations, etc.). Frameworks are filtered by your selected industry and country. Each framework has different PQC adoption deadlines and requirements.

chunks.title: Assessment: Migration Status
chunks.content:
PQC Assessment Wizard — Step 6: Migration Status

The Migration Status step assesses how far along your organization is in the PQC transition: Not Started, Planning, Pilot/Testing, Partial Deployment, or Fully Migrated. Organizations in earlier stages receive higher urgency scores to encourage action.

chunks.title: Assessment: Use Cases
chunks.content:
PQC Assessment Wizard — Step 7: Use Cases

The Use Cases step identifies specific cryptographic applications in your organization: TLS/HTTPS, VPN/IPsec, email signing, code signing, PKI/certificates, IoT device authentication, database encryption, etc. Each use case maps to specific PQC algorithms and migration complexity.

chunks.title: Assessment: Data Retention
chunks.content:
PQC Assessment Wizard — Step 8: Data Retention

Data Retention periods directly impact HNDL risk exposure. Data that must remain confidential for 10+ years (e.g., health records, state secrets, financial archives) faces the highest quantum threat since quantum computers could decrypt it within its retention window. Multiple retention levels can be selected.

chunks.title: Assessment: Credential Lifetime
chunks.content:
PQC Assessment Wizard — Step 9: Credential Lifetime

The Credential Lifetime step assesses how long cryptographic credentials (certificates, keys, tokens) must remain valid in your organization. Long-lived credentials (5+ years) face elevated HNDL/HNFL risk — a certificate valid through 2030 may need to remain trustworthy even after a CRQC arrives. This step drives urgency for PKI migration, code signing transitions, and certificate authority upgrades.

chunks.title: Assessment: Organization Scale
chunks.content:
PQC Assessment Wizard — Step 10: Organization Scale

Organization Scale affects migration complexity and timeline. Large enterprises with thousands of endpoints, multiple data centers, and complex supply chains require longer migration timelines and more comprehensive crypto-agility frameworks than smaller organizations.

chunks.title: Assessment: Crypto Agility
chunks.content:
PQC Assessment Wizard — Step 11: Crypto Agility

Crypto Agility measures your organization's ability to quickly swap cryptographic algorithms. Organizations with centralized key management, automated certificate rotation, and modular crypto libraries can migrate faster. Low agility increases migration risk and timeline.

chunks.title: Assessment: Infrastructure Assessment
chunks.content:
PQC Assessment Wizard — Step 12: Infrastructure Assessment

The Infrastructure step evaluates which systems need PQC upgrades: HSMs, load balancers, firewalls, certificate authorities, databases, cloud services, IoT devices. Hardware-bound systems (HSMs, embedded devices) require longer migration timelines due to firmware/hardware replacement cycles.

chunks.title: Assessment: Target Timeline
chunks.content:
PQC Assessment Wizard — Step 13: Target Timeline

The Target Timeline step sets your organization's PQC migration deadline based on regulatory requirements, risk tolerance, and industry benchmarks. Country-aligned options show relevant national deadlines (e.g., CNSA 2.0 2030/2033 milestones, ANSSI 2025 hybrid requirement).

chunks.title: Getting Started for Developers
chunks.content:
Getting Started with PQC for Developers

Start with the PQC 101 module to understand the quantum threat and why migration matters. Then explore ML-KEM key generation in the Playground — you can generate real PQC keypairs in your browser. The TLS Basics module shows how ML-KEM integrates with TLS 1.3 handshakes. For hands-on practice, OpenSSL Studio provides a full WASM-based OpenSSL 3.6 terminal for generating PQC keys and certificates. The Algorithm Reference page compares all NIST-standardized algorithms with performance benchmarks.

chunks.title: Getting Started for Organizations
chunks.content:
Getting Started with PQC for Organizations

Begin with the Assessment wizard to evaluate your organization's quantum risk posture — it analyzes industry, data sensitivity, compliance requirements, and infrastructure to generate a prioritized migration plan. Review the Compliance page for regulatory frameworks (CNSA 2.0, ANSSI, BSI guidelines) and their deadlines. The Migrate Catalog lists PQC-ready products across 7 infrastructure layers, including HSMs, TLS libraries, and certificate authorities. The Threat Landscape page shows industry-specific quantum risks to help build the business case.

chunks.title: Getting Started for Learners
chunks.content:
Getting Started with PQC for Learners

The Learn section has 75 modules covering PQC fundamentals to advanced topics. Start with PQC 101 for an overview, then Quantum Threats to understand Shor's and Grover's algorithms. Key modules include: Hybrid Cryptography (transition strategy), Crypto Agility (algorithm flexibility), TLS Basics (web security), KMS & PQC, HSM & PQC Operations, Data & Asset Sensitivity, 5G Security, industry-specific modules (Healthcare, Automotive, Aerospace, Energy, EMV Payments), and an executive track (Governance, Business Case, Risk Management, Compliance Strategy, Migration Program). Each module includes interactive demonstrations and a Workshop tab for hands-on exercises. Test your knowledge with the Quiz covering 1,151 questions across 81 categories. The Glossary provides definitions for 100+ PQC terms.

chunks.title: PQC Playground — Interactive Crypto Workshop
chunks.content:
PQC Playground Overview

The PQC Playground (/playground) is a browser-based cryptographic workshop with 34 native interactive tools, 23 Docker-backed sandbox scenarios, an interactive lab, and a full PKCS#11 HSM emulator. Native tools run locally via WebAssembly — no data leaves the browser; sandbox scenarios proxy a real containerized open-source tool.

Six sub-routes:
1. /playground — Workshop grid: searchable catalog of all tools across categories (HSM / PKCS#11, Entropy & Random, Certificates & Proofs, Protocol Simulations, Blockchain & Digital Assets, OpenSSL Studio). Persona-aware filtering with difficulty badges (beginner/intermediate/advanced). Each persona (Executive, Developer, Architect, Researcher, Ops, Curious) sees tailored tool recommendations.
2. /playground/interactive — Interactive lab with 7 tabs: keystore (key generation), data (hex editor), kem_ops (ML-KEM + X25519 ECDH), symmetric (AES/ChaCha), hashing (SHA/SHAKE), sign_verify (PQC + classical signing), logs (operation history with timing).
3. /playground/hsm — PKCS#11 v3.2 HSM playground via SoftHSMv3 WASM with 11 tabs: keystore, kem (standalone ML-KEM encap/decap), symmetric, key_wrap, hashing, sign_verify, key_agree, key_derive, mechanisms, acvp (NIST KAT vectors), logs. Supports C++, Rust, and Dual engine modes with parity cross-check.
4. /playground/cacp — KMIP 3.0 Control Plane: in-browser softhsmrustv3 HSM + crypto-agility policy engine (also reachable at /playground/cacp-kmip).
5. /playground/docker — Docker sandbox launcher: embeds the containerized sandbox environment (pqctoday-sandbox) that backs every sandbox-flagged tool.
6. /playground/:toolId — Individual tool detail pages (both native and sandbox) with lazy-loaded components, breadcrumbs, and endorse/flag buttons.

Supported algorithms: ML-KEM-512/768/1024 (FIPS 203), ML-DSA-44/65/87 (FIPS 204), SLH-DSA all 12 parameter sets (FIPS 205), X25519, P-256, RSA-2048/4096, Ed25519, secp256k1, AES-128/256, ChaCha20. All generated keys are for educational purposes only.

URL deep-linking: ?tab= selects Interactive lab tab (kem_ops, sign_verify, symmetric, hashing, data, keystore, logs). ?algo= pre-selects an algorithm. Combine: /playground/interactive?tab=kem_ops&algo=ML-KEM-768. Every individual tool also has its own /playground/<toolId> deep link — see the per-tool catalog entries.

chunks.title: Playground — 34 Workshop Tools Catalog
chunks.content:
Workshop Tools in the PQC Playground

The workshop grid at /playground lists 34 native interactive tools (plus 23 Docker-sandbox scenarios) organized by category. Each tool has a difficulty level, recommended personas, and its own /playground/<toolId> deep link.

HSM / PKCS#11 (11):
- KMIP Control Plane (advanced) — In-browser KMIP 3.0 control plane + softhsmrustv3 HSM, compiled to WebAssembly. Load a crypto-agility policy (pqc.yaml / classical.yaml), run key lifecycle ops (CreateKeyPair → Activate → Sign / Encap / Decap), and watch the policy auto-rekey a classical ECDSA-P256 key to ML-DSA-65 on the same Sign call — no server, no Docker.
- HSM Capacity Calculator (intermediate) — Explore fictional HSM workloads, utilisation headroom and local redundancy. Preserve per-site inventory and size payment workloads separately; not a production capacity prediction.
- Hybrid KEM + ECDH (intermediate) — ML-KEM + X25519 ECDH + HKDF hybrid encryption pipeline
- Envelope Encryption (intermediate) — ML-KEM + AES key wrap in a KMS envelope encryption pattern
- Multi-Algorithm Signing (intermediate) — Compare ML-DSA, ECDSA, and RSA signing in a token migration workflow
- Firmware Signing (intermediate) — UEFI secure boot firmware signing and verification with ML-DSA-44/65/87 or SLH-DSA (defaults to ML-DSA-65)
- SLH-DSA Sign & Verify (advanced) — All 12 FIPS 205 parameter sets with pre-hash support
- Stateful Hash Signatures (advanced) — LMS and XMSS stateful signature trees using SoftHSMv3
- Hybrid Signature Spectrums (advanced) — Live concatenation, nesting, and Silithium (fused Fiat-Shamir) — from no non-separability to the SNS that Silithium targets
- SP 800-108 KDF (advanced) — NIST SP 800-108 counter-mode key derivation — applicable to KEM secrets, PSK, QKD, and password-derived keys
- TEE-HSM Secure Channel (advanced) — Build a TEE-to-HSM trusted channel with ML-DSA + ML-KEM + AES wrap

Protocol Simulations (6):
- TLS 1.3 Simulator (intermediate) — Client–server TLS 1.3 handshake simulator: configure cipher suites, key exchange groups, mTLS, PQC and hybrid certificates
- PQC VPN Simulator (advanced) — Full IKEv2 handshake in WASM with PKCS#11 crypto routed through softhsmv3. Inspect live C_* calls, ECDH key exchange, and PSK authentication between initiator and responder.
- PQC SSH Simulator (advanced) — Full OpenSSH 10.x handshake in WASM: mlkem768x25519-sha256 KEX + ssh-mldsa-65 host auth + publickey userauth backed by softhsmv3 PKCS#11. Compare classical vs PQC byte sizes and latency.
- 5G SUCI Construction (advanced) — Subscriber identity concealment for 5G: ECDH + ANSI X9.63-KDF + AES (Profiles A/B), plus a post-quantum Profile C using ML-KEM in hybrid and pure modes
- MLS Group Messaging (intermediate) — RFC 9420 TreeKEM visualizer + PKCS#11 provider architecture. Add/remove members, trace re-keyed nodes on each Commit, and see how openmls_pqctoday_crypto routes every crypto op through softhsmv3.
- TPM 2.0 PQC Playground (advanced) — Execute raw TPM 2.0 Post-Quantum operations entirely in the browser using the WebAssembly-compiled pqctpm emulator.

Entropy & Random (5):
- Random Generation (beginner) — Web Crypto + OpenSSL DRBG random generation with statistical analysis
- QRNG Demo (beginner) — Simulation — no QRNG hardware involved. Compares a simulated QRNG sample (crypto.getRandomValues() output, not a quantum source), live Web Crypto output and a deliberately broken PRNG on the same grouped checks, which cannot show whether any source is quantum.
- Entropy Testing (intermediate) — Separate groups: monobit, runs and chi-squared visual checks; the SP 800-90B repetition-count and adaptive-proportion health tests (on samples treated as raw noise-source output); and SHA-256/HMAC primitive self-checks. No SP 800-90B entropy estimate is made here.
- SP 800-90A DRBG (advanced) — Interactive HMAC_DRBG (SHA-256) state machine — Instantiate, Generate, Reseed as specified in NIST SP 800-90A Rev. 1 §10.1.2 — with a known-answer check against pinned NIST ACVP and CAVP vectors.
- Source Combining (advanced) — Two simulated raw sources: SP 800-90B health tests before conditioning, SP 800-90C concatenation (XOR, hash and HMAC as educational variants), Hash_df/SHA-256/HMAC/AES-CMAC conditioning via SoftHSMv3, and an assumption-driven verdict that can end in "not enough evidence" or "unsafe".

Certificates & Proofs (4):
- PKI Workshop (intermediate) — Build a full certificate chain hands-on: CSR → Root CA → cert issuance → parsing → CRL
- Cert Capacity Calculator (beginner) — Estimate certificate-related TLS payload and annual leaf issuance storage for classical and PQC three-level chains. Adjust renewal cadence and encoding assumptions; no CPU prediction.
- Hybrid Certificates (intermediate) — Generate and compare eight X.509 hybrid and post-quantum certificate formats via SoftHSM PKCS#11 + real DER encoding
- Merkle Tree Workshop (intermediate) — Build trees, generate inclusion proofs, verify with tamper detection, compare PQC cert sizes, and simulate Certificate Transparency logs

Digital Identity (1):
- EUDI Wallet Architecture (intermediate) — Complete digital identity lifecycle: Wallet, PID Issuance, Attestation, RP Verification, and QES Provider.

Blockchain & Digital Assets (3):
- Bitcoin Transaction (intermediate) — secp256k1 ECDSA keypair, SHA256 + RIPEMD160, transaction signing
- HD Wallet Derivation (intermediate) — BIP39 mnemonic + BIP32/SLIP-0010 multi-coin HD key derivation
- Solana Transaction (intermediate) — Ed25519 keypair generation and transaction signing

OpenSSL Studio (4):
- OpenSSL Studio (intermediate) — Full OpenSSL v3.6.3 environment: keygen, certificates, CSR, KEM, signing, KDF, encryption — all via WASM
- API Security & JWT Workshop (intermediate) — Sign JWTs with ML-DSA-44/65/87, SLH-DSA, and composite ML-DSA-65+Ed25519 using real @noble/post-quantum or softhsmv3 PKCS#11. Encrypt them as HPKE JWE with ML-KEM-768 or ML-KEM-768 + X25519 per draft-ietf-jose-hpke-encrypt-22 and draft-ietf-jose-hpke-pq-pqt-01, in the browser or entirely inside softhsmv3 (PQCToday candidate CKM_HPKE mechanism).
- PKI Enrollment (EST + CMP) (advanced) — RFC 7030 EST + RFC 4210/9810 CMP — generate an ML-DSA-65 key, run CMP IR against an in-WASM mock CA, verify the issued cert.
- S/MIME & CMS Workshop (advanced) — Real OpenSSL 3.6 WASM CMS SignedData sign+verify (ML-DSA-44/65/87, SLH-DSA, RSA-PSS) and ML-KEM-768 AuthEnvelopedData encrypt+decrypt. Toggle routes signing key through softhsmv3 PKCS#11.

Most tools link back to a corresponding Learn module for deeper education.

chunks.title: Playground — Interactive Lab: KEM & Key Operations
chunks.content:
Interactive Lab — KEM Operations & Key Generation

The PQC Interactive lab at /playground/interactive?tab=kem_ops provides ML-KEM (FIPS 203) hands-on key encapsulation:

KEM Operations tab (?tab=kem_ops) — ML-KEM encapsulation/decapsulation workflow: generate keypair → encapsulate (creates ciphertext + shared secret from public key) → decapsulate (recovers shared secret from private key). Includes X25519 ECDH classical baseline panel for comparison. ML-KEM-768 ciphertext is 1,088 bytes vs X25519 at 32 bytes; shared secret always 32 bytes. Demonstrates quantum-safe key exchange end-to-end.

Keystore tab (?tab=keystore) — Generate keypairs for any supported algorithm (ML-KEM-512/768/1024, ML-DSA-44/65/87, SLH-DSA, X25519, P-256, RSA, Ed25519, secp256k1). Shows public/private key sizes and generation time. Key store persists across tabs within the session.

URL: /playground/interactive?tab=kem_ops&algo=ML-KEM-768 to pre-select ML-KEM-768 for KEM operations.

chunks.title: Playground — Interactive Lab: Sign, Verify & Symmetric
chunks.content:
Interactive Lab — Signing, Verification & Symmetric Crypto

Sign/Verify tab (?tab=sign_verify) — Sign messages with ML-DSA-44/65/87 (FIPS 204), SLH-DSA all 12 parameter sets (FIPS 205), ECDSA, RSA, or Ed25519 private keys; verify with corresponding public keys. Signature size comparison: ML-DSA-65 = 3,309 bytes, SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s = 7,856 bytes, ECDSA P-256 = 64 bytes. LMS stateful-key warning banner included. Pre-select algorithm: /playground/interactive?tab=sign_verify&algo=ML-DSA-65

Symmetric tab (?tab=symmetric) — AES-128/256-GCM, AES-CBC, AES-CTR, AES-CMAC, ChaCha20-Poly1305 encrypt/decrypt operations.

Hashing tab (?tab=hashing) — SHA-256, SHA-512, SHAKE128, SHAKE256 digest computation with hex output.

Data tab (?tab=data) — Hex editor for input data used in subsequent operations.

Logs tab (?tab=logs) — Full operation history with execution times and result status.

chunks.title: Playground — PKCS#11 v3.2 HSM Playground
chunks.content:
PKCS#11 HSM Playground

The HSM Playground at /playground/hsm emulates a PKCS#11 v3.2 hardware security module in the browser using SoftHSMv3 (a fork of SoftHSM2 compiled to WebAssembly). All operations use real PKCS#11 C_ interfaces — mirroring what applications do against hardware HSMs.

Engine modes: C++ (default), Rust, Dual (cross-check where one engine generates and the other verifies for parity validation).

11 tabs:
1. Keystore — Token initialization, HSM key table with generated keys
2. KEM — standalone ML-KEM encapsulate/decapsulate via C_EncapsulateKey/C_DecapsulateKey
3. Symmetric — AES-GCM/CBC/CTR, ChaCha20 encrypt/decrypt via C_EncryptInit/C_Encrypt
4. Key Wrap — AES key wrap/unwrap, AES-GCM wrap, RSA-OAEP wrap via C_WrapKey/C_UnwrapKey
5. Hashing — SHA-256/384/512, SHA3 digests via C_DigestInit/C_Digest
6. Sign/Verify — ML-DSA-44/65/87 and SLH-DSA (all 12 FIPS 205 parameter sets) signing with pre-hash support (SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA3-256, SHA3-384, SHA3-512, SHAKE-128, SHAKE-256, Pure). Classical RSA/ECDSA also available. Uses C_SignInit/C_Sign/C_VerifyInit/C_Verify.
7. Key Agreement — ECDH, X25519 via C_DeriveKey
8. Key Derivation — HKDF (SP 800-56C), PBKDF2 (BIP39 mnemonic to seed) via C_DeriveKey
9. Mechanisms — PKCS#11 mechanism introspection (C_GetMechanismList/C_GetMechanismInfo)
10. ACVP — NIST ACVP Known Answer Test (KAT) vectors for ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA
11. Logs — Full PKCS#11 operation log with C_ function calls, parameters, and timing

Key attributes follow PKCS#11 v3.2 CKA_* conventions: CKA_EXTRACTABLE, CKA_SENSITIVE, CKA_ENCRYPT, CKA_DECRYPT, CKA_WRAP, CKA_UNWRAP, CKA_SIGN, CKA_VERIFY configured via key templates at generation time.

chunks.title: OpenSSL Studio — Browser-Based WASM Terminal
chunks.content:
OpenSSL Studio Overview

OpenSSL Studio provides a full OpenSSL 3.6.1 terminal running in the browser via WebAssembly (WASM). It supports PQC algorithms through the OQS provider, enabling hands-on practice with post-quantum key generation, certificate creation, and cryptographic operations without installing anything. 14 command categories: genpkey, req, x509, enc, dgst, hash, rand, version, files, kem, pkcs12, lms, configutl, kdf. Supports command aliases for user-friendly URLs (keygen→genpkey, sign→dgst, cert→x509, etc.). Embeddable mode hides the page header when used inside workshop tools. All operations execute locally in the browser with SharedArrayBuffer support.

chunks.title: OpenSSL Studio — PQC Key Generation Commands
chunks.content:
PQC Key Generation with OpenSSL Studio

Generate PQC keys using modern OpenSSL 3.x commands:
- ML-KEM: openssl genpkey -algorithm mlkem768 -out mlkem768_key.pem
- ML-DSA: openssl genpkey -algorithm mldsa65 -out mldsa65_key.pem
- SLH-DSA: openssl genpkey -algorithm slhdsa-sha2-128s -out slhdsa_key.pem
- Extract public key: openssl pkey -in key.pem -pubout -out pub.pem

Use genpkey (not genrsa/ecparam) — modern OpenSSL commands support all PQC algorithms through the OQS provider.

chunks.title: OpenSSL Studio — PQC Certificate Operations
chunks.content:
PQC Certificate Operations with OpenSSL Studio

Create PQC certificates and CSRs:
- Self-signed cert: openssl req -x509 -new -key mldsa65_key.pem -out cert.pem -days 365 -subj "/CN=PQC Test"
- CSR: openssl req -new -key mldsa65_key.pem -out csr.pem -subj "/CN=PQC Test"
- Verify cert: openssl x509 -in cert.pem -text -noout
- Sign data: openssl pkeyutl -sign -inkey mldsa65_key.pem -in data.txt -out sig.bin
- Verify signature: openssl pkeyutl -verify -pubin -inkey pub.pem -in data.txt -sigfile sig.bin

All certificates use ML-DSA-65 or other PQC algorithms for signing, demonstrating post-quantum PKI workflows.

chunks.title: Achievement & Badge System Overview
chunks.content:
Achievement & Badge System

PQC Today features a gamification layer with 51 achievement badges across categories (Consistency, Workshop Depth, Cross-Feature) and 4 rarity tiers (Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic). Achievements unlock automatically based on user activity tracked across all stores. Secret achievements add discovery incentive. The system integrates with the 7-belt judo grading system (White → Black belt) and the ScoreCard on the landing page.

Composite awareness score weights: quiz performance, module step completion, artifact generation (keys, certs, CSRs, executive documents), time spent, and streak (consecutive daily visits). Belt thresholds gate based on minimum quiz%, steps%, artifacts, time, and streak per tier.

chunks.title: Judo Belt Grading System — 7 Tiers with Threshold Gates
chunks.content:
Judo Belt Grading System

PQC Today uses a 7-tier judo belt ranking system to measure learning progress. Each belt requires both a minimum composite awareness score AND meeting specific threshold gates (quiz mastery, step completion, artifacts generated, time invested, and daily streak).

Composite Score Formula: Knowledge (40%) + Breadth (30%) + Practice (20%) + Time & Consistency (10%)
- Knowledge: quiz questions correctly answered (cumulative mastery across sessions)
- Breadth: learning module workshop steps completed
- Practice: cryptographic artifacts generated (keys × 8pts, certs × 7pts, CSRs × 5pts, exec docs × 5pts)
- Time & Consistency: total learning minutes (60%) + current daily streak (40%)

Belt Ranks:
- **White Belt** (0–14 pts): "Beginning the journey" — Quiz ≥0%, Steps ≥0%, Artifacts ≥0, Time ≥0min, Streak ≥0 days
- **Yellow Belt** (15–29 pts): "Learning the basics" — Quiz ≥15%, Steps ≥10%, Artifacts ≥0, Time ≥15min, Streak ≥0 days
- **Orange Belt** (30–44 pts): "Exploring foundations" — Quiz ≥30%, Steps ≥25%, Artifacts ≥2, Time ≥45min, Streak ≥0 days
- **Green Belt** (45–59 pts): "Solid fundamentals developing" — Quiz ≥45%, Steps ≥40%, Artifacts ≥3, Time ≥90min, Streak ≥3 days
- **Blue Belt** (60–74 pts): "Building depth consistently" — Quiz ≥60%, Steps ≥60%, Artifacts ≥5, Time ≥180min, Streak ≥4 days
- **Brown Belt** (75–87 pts): "Strong practitioner" — Quiz ≥75%, Steps ≥80%, Artifacts ≥7, Time ≥300min, Streak ≥5 days
- **Black Belt** (88–100 pts): "PQC mastery achieved" — Quiz ≥90%, Steps ≥95%, Artifacts ≥10, Time ≥600min, Streak ≥7 days

Threshold gating: A learner can have the score for Brown Belt but be held at Blue Belt if they haven't generated enough artifacts or maintained a sufficient streak. Unmet gates produce actionable feedback messages (e.g., "Need 2 more artifacts for Brown Belt").

The belt system is persona-scoped: only modules in the active persona's learning path count toward breadth. Quiz mastery is filtered to persona-relevant questions.

chunks.title: Assessment Report: Educational Priority Index
chunks.content:
Assessment Report Section: Educational Priority Index

An educational 0–100 priority index derived from self-reported answers and model defaults. It is not a measured probability, audit grade, or compliance determination.

Wizard Inputs:
  - **Industry (Step 1)**: Determines category weights. For example, government and finance weight regulatory pressure higher, while telecom and energy weight migration complexity higher.
  - **Quantum Exposure inputs**: Algorithms (Step 3), Crypto Use Cases (Step 7), Data Retention (Step 8), Data Sensitivity (Step 4).
  - **Migration Complexity inputs**: Crypto Agility (Step 11), Infrastructure and its nested vendor model (Step 12), System Scale + Team Size (Step 10).
  - **Regulatory Pressure inputs**: Compliance Frameworks (Step 5), Industry (Step 1), Country (Step 2), Timeline Pressure (Step 13). Scope still needs source-level verification.
  - **Organizational Readiness inputs**: Migration Status (Step 9), Team Size (Step 10), Crypto Agility (Step 11), and the nested vendor model in Step 12.
  - **See Risk Breakdown section**: Full per-category weights and situational boosts are documented under the Risk Breakdown info panel.

Scoring Principles:
  • Composite = (QE × w1) + (MC × w2) + (RP × w3) + ((100 − OR) × w4), where OR is readiness (higher is better) and the other categories are attention needs (higher is worse).
  • Situational boosts (up to +20%) are model rules for compounding answer combinations; they are not empirical loss probabilities.
  • Risk level thresholds: Low (0\u201325), Medium (26\u201355), High (56\u201375), Critical (76\u2013100).

chunks.title: Assessment Report: Key Findings
chunks.content:
Assessment Report Section: Key Findings

The 3\u20135 most critical insights automatically identified from your assessment: vulnerable algorithms, compliance gaps, HNDL/HNFL exposure, and migration blockers.

Wizard Inputs:
  - **Algorithms (Step 3)**: Identifies which of your algorithms are quantum-vulnerable.
  - **Compliance (Step 5)**: Flags selected frameworks recorded with PQC requirements or transition targets; selection does not prove applicability.
  - **Data Retention (Step 7) / Credential Lifetime (Step 8)**: Highlights HNDL or HNFL risk windows.
  - **Migration Status (Step 9)**: Flags if migration has not started.

chunks.title: Assessment Report: Risk Breakdown
chunks.content:
Assessment Report Section: Risk Breakdown

Shows four answer-derived model categories. The weights are editorial planning assumptions, not an external benchmark or maturity certification.

Wizard Inputs:
  - **Quantum Exposure**: Algorithms (40%), Use Cases (25%), Data Retention (20%), Data Sensitivity (15%). Measures how exposed your data and operations are to quantum attacks.
  - **Migration Complexity**: Crypto Agility (40%), Infrastructure (30%), System Scale (15%), Vendor Dependency (15%). Measures effort to transition to PQC.
  - **Regulatory Pressure**: Compliance Frameworks (45%), Industry Regulation (30%), Country Urgency + Timeline Pressure (25%). Measures external pressure to migrate.
  - **Organizational Readiness**: Migration Status (40%), Team Capacity (25%), Crypto Agility (20%), Vendor Dependency (15%). Measures your organization’s current ability to execute.

Scoring Principles:
  • Each category is scored 0\u2013100 independently.
  • Category weights are industry-specific (e.g., Finance: QE=0.30, MC=0.25, RP=0.25, OR=0.20).
  • Category drivers (the text under each bar) explain what specifically is pulling each score up or down.

chunks.title: Assessment Report: Executive Summary
chunks.content:
Assessment Report Section: Executive Summary

A narrative summary of your key risks and recommended priorities, written in language tailored to your persona.

Wizard Inputs:
  - **All wizard inputs**: The narrative references selected algorithms, potential requirement-review items, infrastructure answers, and migration status. It does not validate the estate.

chunks.title: Assessment Report: Assessment Profile
chunks.content:
Assessment Report Section: Assessment Profile

A direct snapshot of the selections made in the assessment wizard. No independent evidence or scanning is added.

Wizard Inputs:
  - **All 13 wizard steps**: Industry, Country, Algorithms, Data Sensitivity, Compliance Frameworks, Migration Status, Use Cases, Data Retention, Credential Lifetime, System Scale, Crypto Agility, Infrastructure, Vendor Dependency, Timeline Pressure.

chunks.title: Assessment Report: HNDL & HNFL Risk Windows
chunks.content:
Assessment Report Section: HNDL & HNFL Risk Windows

Compares self-reported retention or credential lifetime with an explicit planning horizon. It illustrates exposure timing; it does not predict CRQC arrival.

Wizard Inputs:
  - **Data Retention (Step 7)**: HNDL: how many years your data must stay confidential. Longer retention = larger risk window.
  - **Credential Lifetime (Step 8)**: HNFL: how many years your signed artifacts must remain trusted. Longer lifetime = larger risk window.
  - **Country (Step 2)**: Adds a separately labelled jurisdiction planning milestone when one is available. It does not change the site-wide CRQC planning assumption used by the HNDL/HNFL illustration.
  - **Algorithms (Step 3)**: HNFL only applies when signing algorithms (RSA, ECDSA, EdDSA) are present.
  - **Use Cases (Step 6)**: Use cases with high HNFL relevance (code signing, PKI, digital identity) are flagged.

Scoring Principles:
  • HNDL attention flag: (current year + retention years) > the site-wide CRQC planning anchor.
  • HNFL attention flag: signing algorithms are present AND (current year + credential lifetime) > the site-wide CRQC planning anchor.
  • Illustrative window = years beyond the CRQC planning anchor; it is not a measured probability or predicted arrival date.
  • “I don’t know” responses use conservative industry defaults (e.g., 75 years for government retention, 10 years for credential lifetime).

chunks.title: Assessment Report: Candidate Algorithm Transitions
chunks.content:
Assessment Report Section: Candidate Algorithm Transitions

Maps each selected primitive to candidate PQC transitions and modelled complexity. The correct choice depends on function, protocol, security category, interoperability and authority.

Wizard Inputs:
  - **Algorithms (Step 3)**: Each selected primitive is looked up for quantum vulnerability and candidate transitions. RSA is dual-use, so its KEM or signature path must be confirmed.
  - **Crypto Agility (Step 11)**: Affects effort estimate — hardcoded crypto means higher migration effort per algorithm.
  - **Infrastructure (Step 12)**: HSM and legacy systems increase migration complexity and effort scope.
  - **Compliance (Step 5)**: Selected sources recorded with PQC requirements increase modelled urgency; applicability requires separate verification.

Scoring Principles:
  • Urgency labels are planning heuristics generated from the answers, not authoritative implementation deadlines.
  • Effort scope: Quick-win, Moderate, Major project, or Multi-year — based on crypto agility and infrastructure complexity.

chunks.title: Assessment Report: Compliance Impact
chunks.content:
Assessment Report Section: Compliance Impact

Shows recorded PQC requirement status and transition targets for selected frameworks, with scope context and source-navigation links.

Wizard Inputs:
  - **Compliance Frameworks (Step 5)**: Each selected framework is looked up for PQC requirement status, targets and notes. The profile filter is educational support, not a legal applicability decision.
  - **Industry (Step 1)**: Filters the available compliance frameworks to those relevant to your industry.
  - **Country (Step 2)**: Country-specific compliance frameworks (e.g., CNSA 2.0 for US) are highlighted.

chunks.title: Assessment Report: Recommended Actions
chunks.content:
Assessment Report Section: Recommended Actions

Prioritized learning and investigation prompts generated from the assessment inputs. Effort labels are coarse model bands, not project estimates.

Wizard Inputs:
  - **Algorithms (Step 3)**: Generates migration actions for each quantum-vulnerable algorithm.
  - **Infrastructure (Step 12)**: Infrastructure-specific actions (e.g., HSM firmware upgrades, PKI re-issuance).
  - **Compliance (Step 5)**: Actions for meeting compliance framework deadlines.
  - **Migration Status (Step 9)**: Actions are prioritized differently based on whether migration has started, is planned, or has not begun.
  - **Crypto Agility (Step 11)**: If hardcoded, an action to introduce an abstraction layer is prioritized.
  - **\u201cI don\u2019t know\u201d responses**: Each unknown generates a specific awareness-gap action recommending an audit of that area.

Scoring Principles:
  • Actions are categorized as Immediate, Short-term, or Long-term based on urgency.
  • Effort levels (Low, Medium, High) are assigned based on scope and infrastructure complexity.
  • Actions are numbered by priority, with the most urgent and impactful first.

chunks.title: Assessment Report: Migration Roadmap
chunks.content:

  - **Country (Step 2)**: The selected jurisdiction’s next sourced milestone is shown as either guidance or a regulatory deadline according to its recorded mandate type.

chunks.title: Assessment Report: Migration Toolkit
chunks.content:

Shows products from the Migrate catalog that match your infrastructure and industry, helping you identify tools for your PQC migration.

Wizard Inputs:
  - **Infrastructure (Step 12)**: Products are filtered to match your selected infrastructure layers and sub-categories (e.g., TLS libraries, PKI platforms, HSM vendors).
  - **Industry (Step 1)**: Products are further filtered by industry relevance.

chunks.title: Assessment Report: ROI Calculator
chunks.content:
Assessment Report Section: ROI Calculator

An illustrative cost/benefit scenario seeded from assessment answers and editorial assumptions. It is not a quote, forecast, regulatory exposure calculation, or finance-approved business case; replace every assumption with organization-specific evidence.

Wizard Inputs:
  - **Algorithm Migrations (Step 3)**: Number of quantum-vulnerable algorithms determines the base engineering cost ($30K per algorithm, scaled by system count).
  - **Infrastructure Layers (Step 12)**: Each selected layer (Hardware, Security Stack, OS, Network, Application, Cloud, Database) adds its estimated migration cost. Hardware/HSM is the most expensive; cloud is the least.
  - **Vendor Dependency (nested in Step 12)**: Heavy vendor dependency increases cost (vendor coordination, licensing, upgrade cycles). Open-source and in-house reduce it.
  - **Migration Status (Step 9)**: Already-started migrations reduce remaining cost to 40%. Planning phase applies 70%. Not-started uses the full estimate.
  - **Crypto Agility (Step 11)**: Hardcoded crypto increases cost by 50% (major refactoring). Fully-abstracted reduces cost by 40%.
  - **Team Size (Step 10)**: Small teams (1\u201310) face 30% higher costs due to longer timelines. Large teams (200+) can parallelize for 15% savings.
  - **Compliance Frameworks (Step 5)**: A rough penalty scenario may be seeded from a selected framework. Selection does not establish applicability, violation, enforcement likelihood, or recoverable savings.
  - **Industry (Step 1)**: Industry breach cost baselines (e.g., Healthcare $9.8M, Finance $6.1M) seed the risk-avoidance benefit calculation.

Scoring Principles:
  • Migration Cost = (Algorithm Base + Infrastructure Base) × Vendor × Migration Status × Agility × Team Size. Floor: $50K.
  • Algorithm Base = Vulnerable algorithm count × $30K × system scale multiplier.
  • Infrastructure Base = sum of per-layer costs for selected layers (Hardware $120K, Security Stack $80K, OS $60K, Network $50K, Application $40K, Database $35K, Cloud $30K).
  • Illustrative avoided-cost scenario = editable scenario probability × industry baseline × planning horizon. The initial probability is a model seed derived from half the priority index and capped at 50%; it is not a measured breach probability.
  • Compliance Savings = compliance penalty per incident × number of PQC-mandating frameworks. Penalty seeded from the highest framework-specific baseline.
  • Net ROI = ((Avoided Breach Cost + Compliance Savings − Migration Cost) / Migration Cost) × 100%.
  • Payback Period = Migration Cost / (Total Benefit / 12 months).

chunks.title: Assessment Report: KPI Trending
chunks.content:
Assessment Report Section: KPI Trending

Compares the educational priority index and category values across multiple self-assessments. Each completion saves a model snapshot. The line chart plots index history, while the radar chart compares current category values with the previous snapshot; neither proves migration progress.

Wizard Inputs:
  - **Assessment History**: Each completed assessment saves the educational priority index, model band, and four category values. Up to five snapshots are retained.
  - **All wizard inputs (indirectly)**: Each snapshot captures the computed priority index and category values at completion time. Changing answers and completing again creates a new model snapshot.

Scoring Principles:
  • Line chart: plots each snapshot’s educational priority index (0\u2013100). Reference lines at 70 and 40 show editorial model-band thresholds, not externally validated risk thresholds.
  • Radar chart: overlays your current four category scores (Quantum Exposure, Migration Complexity, Regulatory Pressure, Org Readiness) against the previous assessment’s scores.
  • Delta badge: the colored pill under the priority gauge shows the point change since the previous self-assessment (− green, + red); it reflects answer/model changes, not measured risk reduction.
  • The line chart requires at least 2 completed assessments to appear. The radar chart shows from the first assessment onward.
  • History is preserved when you reset and re-take the assessment so you can compare model snapshots over time.

chunks.title: Assessment Report: Industry Threat Landscape
chunks.content:

Shows industry-specific quantum threats matched against your current algorithms, sourced from the Threats database.

Wizard Inputs:
  - **Industry (Step 1)**: Filters threats to your industry. Each industry has a specific set of quantum threat scenarios.
  - **Algorithms (Step 3)**: Threats are matched against your selected algorithms to highlight which are relevant to your stack.

chunks.title: Assessment Report: Country PQC Timeline
chunks.content:

Displays sourced PQC milestones for the selected jurisdiction, distinguishing binding requirements from guidance where the data supports that distinction.

Wizard Inputs:
  - **Country (Step 2)**: Determines which jurisdiction timeline is shown. A published target is not automatically a legal deadline for every organization.

chunks.title: Business Center / Command Center — CSWP.39 5-step PQC Operating Dashboard
chunks.content:
Business Center / Command Center (/business) Overview

The Command Center is the executive PQC operating dashboard, organised around the NIST CSWP.39 (Dec 2025) 5-step process: Govern → Inventory → Identify Gaps → Prioritise → Implement. Each step renders as a card with artifacts, a deterministic Tier badge, and links into the underlying Compliance and Migrate views. Reorganised in v3.5.8 from the previous 7-pillar layout.

Three routes:
- /business — Command Center dashboard, fixed 5-step stack + cross-cut strips
- /business/tools — Searchable catalogue of business planning tools
- /business/tools/:toolId — Individual tool detail page with lazy-loaded component

Five CSWP.39 steps (always rendered in 1→5 order; persona only drives which step expands by default):
1. Govern (§5.1–5.4, Governance pillar) — crypto policy, RACI, standards-watch subscriptions, partner ecosystem register, exception-handling workflow
2. Inventory (§5.2, Inventory pillar) — CBOM across six asset classes (Code, Libraries, Applications, Files, Protocols, Systems) with SBOM/CMDB ingestion, criticality + sensitivity metadata, ESV (SP 800-90B) status alongside FIPS 140-3
3. Identify Gaps (§5.3, Observability pillar) — crypto scanners, vulnerability mgmt, asset mgmt, SIEM crypto-drift logging, Zero-Trust enforcement, data classification
4. Prioritise (§5.4, Assurance pillar) — risk-analysis prioritisation engine, scoring model, Critical/High/Medium/Low queue, monthly KPIs, feedback loop to Governance
5. Implement — Mitigate or Migrate (§4.6 / §5.5, Lifecycle pillar) — crypto-agility assessment per asset, ML-KEM-768 / ML-DSA-65 / SLH-DSA migration paths, gateway mitigation with mandatory sunset (§4.6: 'Mitigation is not a permanent solution'), evidence artefacts (CMVP cert, ACVP run, CVE-scan)

Tier badges: each step shows a TierBadge (Partial / Risk-Informed / Repeatable / Adaptive) computed deterministically from existing artifacts and section markers via pure functions in src/components/BusinessCenter/lib/cswp39Tier.ts. Hover the badge for the contributing-artifacts tooltip.

Three cross-cut strips:
- Action Items (top) — outstanding tasks across all 5 steps
- Cyber Insurance Lens (togglable side panel) — premium-impact view per step; expanded by default for executive persona
- Learning Bar (bottom) — recommended Learn modules linked to the active step

Persona emphasis (BC_STEP_EMPHASIS_BY_PERSONA in src/data/personaConfig.ts): executive opens on Govern with insurance panel open; architect opens on Identify Gaps; ops opens on Implement.

Artifact management: each step has STEP_ARTIFACT_TYPES mapping in src/components/BusinessCenter/lib/cswp39StepMapping.ts. Existing artifacts render as ArtifactCard (View/Edit/Delete actions); missing artifacts render as ArtifactPlaceholder with a 'Create' link to the source Learn module. Artifacts are persisted by ExecutiveDocumentType. Export ZIP functionality groups artifacts by step.

Maturity Evidence Grid linkage: the matching tier row in /compliance?tab=cswp39 deep-links from each step's Tier badge, so users can pivot from 'where am I' to 'what evidence exists at my tier'. Backed by pqc_maturity_governance_requirements_*.csv (~176 requirements at maturity levels 2 and 3 across pillars).

chunks.title: Business Center — 37 Planning Tools
chunks.content:
Business Planning Tools (/business/tools)

The Business Center includes 37 interactive planning tools organized into 5 categories. Access via the Tools tab at /business/tools. Each tool generates executive artifacts that appear in the dashboard.

Risk & Strategy (9 tools):
- ROI Calculator — Calculate migration ROI with breach avoidance, compliance savings, and payback period
- Board Pitch Builder — Build board-ready investment proposals with executive summary and budget request
- Breach Scenario Simulator — Compare classical vs quantum-enabled breach cost (per-event and annual expected loss) with HNDL exposure
- Cost of Inaction Analyzer — Compare the discounted cost of starting now with delaying PQC migration, with assumptions and uncertainty visible
- Cost Model Explorer — Compare the six PQC costing-model families on one scenario, with a live Monte Carlo run
- CRQC Scenario Planner — Plan for cryptographically relevant quantum computer threat scenarios
- Risk Register Builder — Build a PQC risk register with current algorithm, threat vector, likelihood, impact and mitigation
- Risk Heatmap & Treatment Plan — Visualise residual risk and draft treatment strategies per risk category
- Initial Scoping Assessment — Phase 0 first-cut scope — top-20 in-scope systems, an estate-size estimate, and the top-10 vendor dependencies; seedable from your /migrate selection

Compliance & Audit (3 tools):
- Compliance Checklist — Per-framework PQC compliance checklist seeded from your starred frameworks and assessment
- Audit Readiness Checklist — Multi-section audit checklist covering inventory, policy, controls, and documentation
- Compliance Timeline Builder — Plot framework milestones, deadlines, and dependencies on a single timeline

Governance & Policy (6 tools):
- RACI Builder — Build RACI matrices for 10 PQC activities across 6 organizational roles
- Policy Template Generator — Generate cryptographic algorithm, key management, vendor, and migration policies
- KPI Dashboard Builder — Build KPI dashboards for tracking PQC migration metrics and progress
- Program Charter — Phase 0 mandate artifact — sponsor sign-off, Steering Committee, QRPM appointment, governance cadence, and the multi-year budget commitment
- Skills & Team Plan — Foundations staffing plan — core roles + FTE from the framework role model, the 1-FTE-per-500-instances sizing heuristic, and build / borrow / buy per role
- Accelerated Execution Profile — Phase 4 Activity 4.7 — a pre-drafted contingency package (trigger conditions, compressed sequence, pre-approved risk acceptances, emergency resource request, activation authority) activated if the quantum timeline accelerates

Vendor & Supply Chain (3 tools):
- Vendor Scorecard Builder — Create vendor assessment scorecards for PQC readiness evaluation
- Contract Clause Generator — Generate PQC-ready contract clauses for vendor agreements
- Supply Chain Risk Matrix — Assess supply chain risks with dependency mapping and impact analysis

Migration Planning (16 tools):
- Roadmap Builder — Build a two-track migration roadmap (key-exchange/HNDL ∥ signatures-PKI/TNFL) on the 8-phase spine, with gates G0–G6 (+ G8 at closure) and milestone dependencies
- Stakeholder Comms Planner — Plan stakeholder communication strategies for PQC migration programs
- KPI Tracker Template — Track migration KPIs with configurable metrics and reporting templates
- Deployment Playbook — Generate deployment playbooks with rollback procedures and validation steps
- Hybrid Transition Planner — Architect-facing decision tree from CSWP.39 §3.2.4 - pick traditional+PQC, PQC+PQC, pure PQC, or crypto-gateway pathway with concrete algorithm pairings
- MTI Negotiator — Protocol-designer + architect decision tool from CSWP.39 §3.1.1 - picks Mandatory-to-Implement signature / KEM / hash plus alternates from audience, deadline, and constraint inputs
- Crypto API Refactor Audit — Architect + senior-developer audit from CSWP.39 §4.1 - grades current crypto-agility state and emits a phased refactor checklist with language-specific call-site guidance (Go / Java / .NET / Node / Python / Rust / C / C++ / JS)
- Cloud Responsibility Matrix — Architect + compliance-lead matrix from CSWP.39 §6.4 - per-asset-class shared-responsibility model across IaaS / PaaS / SaaS / FaaS, with PQC availability per cloud and watch-outs for multi-cloud, BYOK, FedRAMP, and sovereign-cloud overlays
- Crypto Architecture Diagram — Document apps, libraries, HSMs, protocols, key stores, and CAs with their dependencies; renders as a Mermaid diagram
- Management Tools Audit — Audit your discovery, assessment, configuration, and enforcement tooling stack — feeds the Information Repository per CSWP.39 §5
- Crypto BOM (CBOM) Builder — Build a CBOM slice from an SBOM, library posture, or HSM inventory; feeds the Assets pipeline
- Crypto Vulnerability Watch — NIST NVD CVE digest for the products on your /migrate selection, joined via CPE — the top CVEs per product by severity from the current snapshot
- Infrastructure Modernization Planner — Phase 6 deliverable — consolidates the PKI modernization plan, HSM/KMS upgrade schedule, network/middlebox compatibility report, and PQC capacity plan into one infrastructure-readiness artifact
- Refresh-Cycle Alignment — Phase 4 Activity 4.3 — maps PQC migration tasks onto already-funded infrastructure refresh programs (data center, SD-WAN, cloud, PKI, HSM, vendor renewals) so PQC work rides existing budgets
- Data-at-Rest Strategy — Phase 5 Activity 5.6 — per-store data-at-rest decision (re-encrypt under PQC keys, PQC key-wrap, crypto-shred, delete, or accept & monitor), recorded back into the CBOM
- Migration Verification & Closure — Prove migration with the framework's 5-point evidence standard, log classical-key decommissioning (SP 800-88), and record program closure & BAU handover

The tools grid supports search (across name, description, keywords, category) and category filter pills with counts. Each tool page includes breadcrumb navigation (Category / Tool Name) and endorse/flag buttons for community validation.

chunks.title: Right Panel — PQC Assistant + Learning Journey
chunks.content:
Right Panel Overview

The Right Panel is a slide-over drawer (60vw on desktop, full-width on mobile) accessible from every page via the floating action button (z-60). Two tabs (the previous 'Graph' / Knowledge Graph tab was removed in v3.5.10–v3.5.11 and no longer exists; useRightPanelStore v2→v3 migration reroutes any persisted activeTab='graph' to 'chat'):

1. **Assistant** (Bot icon) — PQC Assistant chatbot (BYOK Gemini API key, RAG-powered over the rag-corpus.json corpus). Context-aware of current page, persona, industry, and assessment results. Conversation history persisted via useChatStore.

2. **Journey** (Clock icon) — Persona-aware view:
   - With persona selected: JourneyMapPanel showing learning path phases, milestone checkpoints, belt progression visual (White → Black), achievement badge grid, off-the-beaten-path module suggestions, and recent activity feed
   - Without persona: ProgressDashboard with belt/score display, track completion pills, stats row (streak, total time, keys generated, certs created, executive docs), assessment status card, and 30-day streak calendar

Keyboard: Escape closes panel. Body scroll locked while open.

chunks.title: Guided Tour — 3-Phase Onboarding
chunks.content:
Guided Tour Overview

First-time visitors see a 3-phase guided tour overlay that introduces the platform. The tour uses centered swipeable cards (Framer Motion drag gestures) and can be dismissed at any time. Completion is persisted to localStorage ('pqc-tour-completed'). Adding ?tour to any URL resets the tour for re-entry.

Phase 1: Why PQC? (3 educational slides)
1. 'Everything runs on encryption' — RSA/ECC depend on classical math
2. 'Quantum computers change everything' — Shor's algorithm breaks them; Harvest Now, Decrypt Later is already happening
3. 'The solution exists — the race is on' — NIST PQC standards published 2024, government mandates 2030-2035

Phase 2: Knowledge Gate
After the intro, users choose: 'I'm new to this' (full feature tour, 14 slides) or 'I know the basics' (essential-only subset of 6 slides).

Phase 3: Feature Tour (up to 14 slides, persona-filtered)
Only pages accessible to the current persona are shown. Features covered: Learning Modules, Migration Timeline, Algorithm Explorer, Migrate Catalog, Compliance Tracker, Risk Assessment, Readiness Report, Crypto Playground, OpenSSL Studio, Threat Landscape, Standards Library, Industry Leaders, PQC Assistant, Glossary.

Essential slides (shown in both modes): Learning Modules, Migration Timeline, Risk Assessment, Readiness Report, PQC Assistant, Glossary.

chunks.title: Landing Page — Platform Overview & Persona Selection
chunks.content:
PQC Today Landing Page

The landing page introduces the PQC adoption lifecycle through a 12-step journey grouped into 4 sections: Start the Journey (Learn, Timeline, Algorithms), My Journey (Migrate, Compliance), Assess & Report (Assess, Report, Business Center, Test & Build), and Keep Up to Date (Threats, Library, Leaders). Users select a persona (Executive, Developer, Architect, Researcher, IT Ops/DevOps, or Curious Explorer) to personalize their experience — each persona sees "For you" badges on recommended journey steps and receives tailored recommendations throughout the platform.

Key statistics displayed: 75 interactive learning modules, 1,151 quiz questions in 81 categories, 128 algorithms catalogued, 897 products in the migration catalog, a 13-step quantum risk assessment wizard, and compliance deadlines spanning 2024–2036. The Business Center adds 37 planning tools.

The ScoreCard tracks learning progress using a judo belt grading system (White through Black belt) based on module completions and quiz performance. Context-aware CTAs evolve based on progress: "View Your Report" after assessment completion, "Continue Your Journey" if learning started. There is no sign-in control in the app today, and Google Drive sync is built into the code but is not currently available.

PQC Today is open source (GPL-3.0) and has no backend, database or user accounts of its own — all cryptographic operations run in the browser using WebAssembly (OpenSSL v3.6.1 + liboqs-js v0.15.1). Google Analytics 4 runs on every visit and records page views and interaction events; text typed into search boxes is scrubbed of personal data before it is sent. The About page (Data Privacy) and the Terms of Service (/terms) say what is recorded and how to block it.

chunks.title: Timeline Page — Global PQC Migration Milestones
chunks.content:
Timeline Page Overview

The Timeline page displays a Gantt chart of global PQC migration milestones for 50+ countries from 2024 to 2035. Events are categorized into 10 phase types: Discovery (cryptographic inventory), Testing (pilot deployments), POC (proof of concept), Migration (live deployment), Standardization (new PQC standards), Guidance (advisories), Policy (regulations enacted), Regulation (compliance enforcement), Research (ongoing development), and Deadline (hard cutoff dates).

Event categories: Milestones (singular achievements like a standard publication) and Phases (multi-year transitions like a country's migration period).

Filter by: text search, country selection, phase type, event type, and region (Americas, EMEA, Asia-Pacific, Global/International). When a specific country is selected, a DocumentTable appears below the Gantt chart showing detailed entries with organization, phase badge, type, title, period, description, and source link.

Key deadlines: Australia 2030 (most aggressive), Canada 2026/2031/2035, UK 2028 (3-phase), Czech Republic 2027 (first EU-specific), EU 2030/2035, Israel 2025, Taiwan 2027, Germany 2030 (QUANTITY initiative), G7 2034 (financial sector), CNSA 2.0 2030 exclusive/2035 full.

URL filter parameters:
- ?event=<event_id> — open one specific milestone/phase (its stable event_id; event titles are still accepted)
- ?region=<region> — filter by region: americas | eu | apac | global (omit for All Regions)
- ?country=<countryName> — filter to a specific country (e.g., /timeline?country=United+States); when present, region defaults to All
- ?q=<text> — search/filter within the Gantt chart
- ?phase=<phase type> — filter by phase type (e.g., Migration, Testing); ?deadlines=1 shows deadline bars only
- ?cat=government|standards|vendor — issuing organisation's category, repeatable (default: government + standards); it is not the phase type

Example links: /timeline?region=eu (EU countries only), /timeline?country=Germany (Germany timeline only), /timeline?region=apac&country=Japan (Japan within APAC view), /timeline?q=FIPS (search for FIPS events).

chunks.title: Algorithms Page — Transition Guide & Detailed Comparison
chunks.content:
Algorithms Page Overview

The Algorithms page has four tabs: Transition Guide (default) shows classical → PQC migration paths (e.g., RSA-2048 → ML-KEM-768 + ML-DSA-65); Detailed Comparison is a flat, sortable table with full specs for every algorithm, with a Browse ↔ Compare toggle; Protocol Support (the PQC Protocol Matrix) tracks IETF/TCG/OASIS/3GPP/IEEE/UEFI protocol standardization across 4 PQC dimensions (pure-KEM, hybrid-KEM, pure-Sig, hybrid-Sig) in a Heatmap or Detailed card view; Validation runs live in-browser KAT (known-answer-test) vectors and documents implementation-level attacks (side-channel, fault injection, RNG). A baseline algorithm is auto-selected for Detailed-tab comparisons: ECDH P-256 for KEM families, RSA-2048 for Signature families.

PQC algorithm families: ML-KEM (FIPS 203, lattice-based KEM — 512/768/1024 parameter sets), ML-DSA (FIPS 204, lattice-based signatures — 44/65/87), SLH-DSA (FIPS 205, stateless hash-based signatures — 12 variants), FN-DSA (planned FIPS 206; in development with no public draft or final publication; compact lattice signatures — 512/1024), HQC (code-based KEM, NIST Round 4 backup), FrodoKEM (conservative LWE, not standardized), Classic McEliece (large keys, impractical), LMS/XMSS (SP 800-208, stateful hash-based, firmware signing).

Classical algorithms shown as deprecated: RSA (all sizes), ECDSA (P-256/384/521), ECDH (X25519/X448), EdDSA — all vulnerable to Shor's algorithm.

NIST Security Levels: L1 (AES-128), L2 (SHA-256 collision), L3 (AES-192), L4 (SHA-384 collision), L5 (AES-256). Data per algorithm: security level, AES equivalent, public/private key sizes, signature/ciphertext size, performance benchmarks, stack RAM, FIPS status, use case notes.

chunks.title: Library Page — Standards, RFCs & Reference Documents
chunks.content:
Library Page Overview

The Library catalogs 680+ technical standards, RFCs, and reference documents for PQC. Documents are organized across 10 categories (Digital Signature, KEM, PKI Certificate Management, Protocols, Government & Policy, NIST Standards, International Frameworks, Migration Guidance, Algorithm Specifications, Industry & Research) and filterable by organization and sector. Persona-aware category boosting surfaces the most relevant categories for your role.

Published key standards: FIPS 203 (ML-KEM), FIPS 204 (ML-DSA), FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA), NIST IR 8547 (transition guidance, deprecate 2030/disallow 2035), and SP 800-208 (LMS/XMSS). Planned FIPS 206 (FN-DSA) remains in development; NIST has not published an Initial Public Draft or final standard.

Recent RFCs: RFC 9629 (KEM in CMS), RFC 9708 (HSS/LMS in CMS), RFC 9802 (HSS/XMSS in X.509), RFC 9814 (SLH-DSA in CMS), RFC 9881/9882 (ML-DSA in X.509 and CMS), RFC 8784 (PQC PSK for IKEv2).

Regional standards: ETSI TS 103 744 (EU hybrid KEM), BSI TR-02102 (Germany), ANSSI Position Paper (France hybrid mandate), CCCS ITSM.40.001 (Canada), ASD ISM-1917 (Australia).

Cross-reference system: Library documents link to compliance frameworks (via libraryRefs), timeline events (via timelineRefs), and inter-document dependencies.

URL filter parameters (all combinable, produce shareable links):
- ?ref=<referenceId> — open a specific document detail panel; the id is the exact reference_id, spaces included (e.g., /library?ref=FIPS%20203)
- ?cat=<category> — filter by category: Digital Signature | KEM | PKI Certificate Management | Protocols | Government & Policy | NIST Standards | International Frameworks | Migration Guidance | Algorithm Specifications | Industry & Research | Compliance & Certification | Blockchain Standards | Implementations
- ?org=<organization> — filter by standardization body: NIST, IETF, ETSI, 3GPP, ENISA, NSA, CISA/NSA, ANSSI France, BSI Germany, UK NCSC, CCCS Canada, ASD Australia, CA/Browser Forum, Cloud Security Alliance, CRYPTREC Japan, Open Quantum Safe
- ?sector=<NAICS code> — filter by sector (repeatable): 52 Finance & Insurance | 92 Public Administration | 54 Professional & Technical Services | 51 Information Technology | 62 Healthcare & Life Sciences | 22 Energy & Utilities | 48 Transportation | 91 Government & Defense
- ?sort=<order> — sort: published (publication date; the default with no role set) | newest (recently updated) | name | referenceId | urgency | mostCited
- ?view=<mode> — layout: cards (default) | table

Example shareable links: /library?cat=KEM&org=NIST (NIST KEM standards), /library?cat=Digital+Signature&sort=urgency (signature docs by urgency), /library?sector=52&cat=Protocols (finance protocol standards), /library?ref=FIPS%20203&cat=KEM (open ML-KEM doc with KEM filter active).

chunks.title: Threats Page — Industry-Specific Quantum Risk Dashboard
chunks.content:
Threats Page Overview

The Threats dashboard lists 71 quantum threat scenarios across 15 industries: Aerospace / Aviation / Space, Cloud Computing / Data Centers, Critical Infrastructure / OT, Cross-Industry, Cryptocurrency / Blockchain, Education / Research, Finance & Banking, Government & Defense, Healthcare / Pharmaceutical, Insurance, Internet of Things (IoT), IT Industry / Software, Media / Entertainment / DRM, Payment Card Industry, Telecommunications.

Criticality levels in use: Critical, High, Medium, Low. A row whose criticality has not been assessed shows as Unrated.

Key concepts:
- HNDL (Harvest Now, Decrypt Later): adversaries capture encrypted data today to decrypt once a cryptographically relevant quantum computer (CRQC) exists — a confidentiality threat.
- HNFL / TNFL (Harvest/Tamper Now, Forge Later): adversaries plan to forge signatures (code signing, certificates, legal documents) once ECDSA/RSA fall — an authenticity threat.
- Each threat carries a reviewed class — HNDL, HNFL/TNFL, or both — and a Shor-resource tier graded from its at-risk cryptography (Imminent, Near-term, Grover-weakened, PQC-safe, or Unscored when no algorithm is named).

Each threat entry shows: threat ID, industry, description, criticality, cryptography at risk, recommended PQC replacement, source with its evidence (whether the cited document is confirmed to be the one named, how many of the entry’s claims it states, approved second sources, last verified), trust score, the SOC detection use cases and incident-response playbooks that apply to its class (Applied Quantum PQC Migration Framework v3.0), and related learning modules. The page also carries the CRQC Threat Horizon (the published CRQC expert forecast window, regulators’ migration deadlines shown separately as deadlines, and per-sector Mosca deadlines).

URL parameters (all combinable):
- ?id=<threatId> — open one threat's detail (e.g. /threats?id=AERO-002); a retired id shows when and why it was retired
- ?industry=<name> — industry filter, comma-separated for several (e.g. /threats?industry=Aerospace%20%2F%20Aviation%20%2F%20Space)
- ?criticality=<level> — Critical | High | Medium | Low
- ?class=<hndl|hnfl> — threat class; hndl shows threats classed HNDL or both, hnfl shows HNFL/TNFL or both
- ?q=<text> — search threat IDs, descriptions, industries, cryptography at risk and PQC replacements
- ?sort=<industry|threatId|criticality|evidence> — sort field (default industry; evidence = best-evidenced first: source confirmed, claims the cited document states)
- ?dir=<asc|desc> — sort direction (default asc)
- ?mode=<table|cards> — layout (default table)
- ?tier=<Authoritative|High|Moderate|Low> — trust-tier filter, repeatable
- ?view=horizon — open scrolled to the CRQC Threat Horizon section

Example links: /threats?criticality=Critical&class=hndl (critical decrypt-later threats), /threats?id=AERO-002 (open one threat), /threats?sort=evidence&dir=desc (best-evidenced first), /threats?view=horizon (CRQC Threat Horizon).

chunks.title: Compliance Page — Regulatory Frameworks & Deadline Tracking
chunks.content:
Compliance Page Overview

The Compliance page tracks 48+ regulatory frameworks, certifications, and mandates affecting PQC migration.

Framework types:
- Cryptographic Module Validation: FIPS 140-3 (US/CMVP), KCMVP (Korea)
- Algorithm Validation: ACVP (NIST test vectors)
- International Evaluation: Common Criteria (ISO/IEC 15408), EUCC v2.0
- Government Mandates: CNSA 2.0 (NSA), ASD ISM (Australia), CCCS (Canada), NCSC (UK), NZISM (NZ)
- EU Regulations: EU Recommendation 2024/1101, eIDAS 2.0 (digital identity wallets 2027+), DORA (financial resilience, enforced Jan 2025), NIS2 (transposition Oct 2024)
- Regional Standards: ANSSI (France, phased 2025–2030), BSI TR-02102 (Germany), CRYPTREC (Japan), KpqC (Korea, 2029/2035), OSCCA NGCC (China)
- Industry-Specific: PCI-DSS (payments), HIPAA (healthcare), GSMA NG.116 (mobile 2026–2028), NERC-CIP (power grid), IEC 62443 (industrial), DO-326A (aviation), ISO/SAE 21434 (automotive)

CNSA 2.0 key deadlines: software/firmware signing preferred 2025, exclusive 2030; networking equipment preferred 2026; NSS acquisitions exclusive 2027; web/cloud exclusive 2033; full transition 2035.

Each framework entry shows: ID, description, industries affected, countries/regions, PQC required status, deadline, enforcement body, and cross-references to Library standards and Timeline events.

URL deep links: ?framework=<id> opens one framework's detail drawer (e.g., /compliance?framework=CNSA-2); ?tab=obligations | requirements | progress | products | foryou | standards (standardization bodies) | certification (FIPS/ACVP/CC schemes) | compliance (regulatory frameworks) | records (FIPS/ACVP/CC product certification records) | cswp39 (CSWP.39 maturity evidence); ?cert=<recordId> opens a specific certification record directly (implies tab=records); ?evref=<library ref> opens a CSWP.39 evidence reference (implies tab=cswp39); ?q=<text> filters certification records; ?pqc=<algorithm name> filters records by PQC algorithm (e.g., ML-KEM); ?mcat=<category> filters cert records by module category (comma-separated for multiple); ?org=, ?ind=, ?region=, ?country= filter landscape tabs.

chunks.title: Migrate Page — 7-Phase Framework & Software Catalog
chunks.content:
Migrate Page Overview

The Migrate page provides a 7-phase PQC migration framework aligned with NIST, NSA CNSA 2.0, CISA, and ETSI guidance:
1. Assess — Build Cryptographic Bill of Materials (CBOM), identify quantum-vulnerable algorithms
2. Plan — Classify data by confidentiality lifetime, map regulatory deadlines, create migration priority matrix
3. Prepare — Select PQC libraries (OpenSSL 3.5+, AWS-LC, BoringSSL), upgrade HSM firmware, engage vendor roadmaps
4. Test — Pilot hybrid TLS/SSH with ML-KEM + X25519, test VPN PQC tunnels, measure performance impact
5. Migrate — Deploy hybrid certificates, migrate code signing to ML-DSA/SLH-DSA, update key management
6. Launch — Complete disk/database encryption migration, update secure boot chains, re-encrypt archived data (HNDL counter-measures)
7. Ramp Up — Deploy continuous crypto monitoring, deprecate legacy algorithms, optimize performance

Software catalog: 897 products in the migration catalog, organized across 9 infrastructure layers (Cloud, Network, Application Servers, Libraries & SDKs, Security Software, Database, Security Stack, Operating Systems, Hardware & Secure Elements).

Three view modes: Stack (default, grouped by infrastructure layer with expandable rows), Cards (flat grid), and Table (sortable columns). Three-tier FIPS badge system: Validated (green, FIPS 140-3), Partial (amber, FedRAMP/WebTrust/FIPS-mode claims), No (gray). Certification cross-reference links products to FIPS/ACVP/Common Criteria certifications. Community members can submit product update requests via contribution cards.

URL parameters (produce shareable links):
- ?tab=<replace|plan|roadmaps|vendorrisk> — workbench tab: Replace what you own | Plan & sequence | Vendor roadmaps | Vendor risk
- ?product=<product_id> — open and expand one product (exact product name also accepted), e.g. /migrate?product=btq-bitcoin-quantum
- ?productIds=<id,id> — show exactly these products
- ?domain=<domain id> — Replace-tab infrastructure domain
- ?vendor=<VND id> — with tab=roadmaps, open one vendor's PQC roadmap (e.g., /migrate?tab=roadmaps&vendor=VND-089)

chunks.title: Assess Page — 13-Step Quantum Risk Assessment Wizard
chunks.content:
Assess Page Overview

The Assess page provides a personalized PQC risk assessment with two modes: Quick (6 steps, ~2 min) for rapid baseline, and Comprehensive (13 steps, ~5 min) for detailed migration planning.

13 comprehensive steps: Industry → Country → Crypto Stack → Data Sensitivity → Compliance → Migration Status → Use Cases → Data Retention → Credential Lifetime → Organization Scale → Crypto Agility → Infrastructure → Timeline Pressure.

Key features:
- Country selection drives compliance deadline alignment and framework filtering
- Data Sensitivity and Data Retention are multi-select with worst-case (max) scoring for HNDL risk
- HNDL window = data retention period minus estimated time to CRQC
- Industry selection filters compliance frameworks to show only relevant regulations
- Persona-aware report recommendations (Executive/Developer/Architect/Researcher/IT Ops)
- Auto-seeds industry and country from persona store if available

Four risk categories scored: Strategic Risk (long-term quantum exposure), Operational Risk (system complexity), Compliance Risk (regulatory deadline pressure), Vendor Risk (third-party dependency control).

Report includes deep links to Migrate products, Timeline events, Compliance frameworks, and Learn modules tailored to your results. Supports Print/PDF output. Progress auto-saves to localStorage with resume capability.

Use ?step= to deep-link to specific steps (e.g., /assess?step=3 for Data Sensitivity).

chunks.title: About Page — Platform Details, SBOM, Privacy & Licensing
chunks.content:
About Page Overview

The About page provides comprehensive platform information across 14 sections: Release Notes, Vision, Transparency, Cloud Sync & Privacy, Community, Data Foundation, Trust Score Methodology, SBOM, Security Audit, Data Privacy, License, RAG AI, Crypto Buff (achievements), and Appearance (theme settings).

Software Bill of Materials (SBOM): React v19, Tailwind CSS v4, Framer Motion (animations), Lucide React (icons), React Router v7. Crypto stack: OpenSSL WASM v3.6.1 (primary), @oqs/liboqs-js v0.15.1 (PQC algorithms), @noble/curves and @scure/* (blockchain crypto), Web Crypto API (X25519, P-256). State management: Zustand with localStorage persistence. Data: PapaParse (CSV), Recharts (visualization). Testing: Vitest + Playwright + axe-playwright (accessibility). Build: Vite + TypeScript strict mode.

Security Audit: 0 production vulnerabilities. Dev-only findings are ESLint toolchain ReDoS (minimatch, ajv) — don't affect deployed app.

Data Privacy: Static site with no backend, database or user accounts of its own; PQC Today does not ask for a name, email address or account details. Google Analytics 4 runs on every visit: it records page views and interaction events (for example which learning modules are started or completed, and searches), sets cookies that give the browser a random identifier, and Google also receives the visitor's IP address. Text typed into search boxes is scrubbed of personal data (email addresses, web addresses, IP addresses and long key-like strings) before it is sent. Analytics are off on localhost, and can be blocked with a content blocker for google-analytics.com, by blocking cookies for the site, or with Google's opt-out browser add-on. Preferences, assessment results, saved assessments and learning progress are kept in the browser's localStorage and PQC Today does not receive them; they leave the browser only if the user shares a report link or uses the PQC Assistant's Gemini cloud mode. Google Drive sync is built into the code but is not currently available (there is no sign-in control in the app today). All cryptography runs client-side via WebAssembly. Chat messages go to Google only when the PQC Assistant is used in cloud (Gemini) mode with the user's own API key; the Local LLM mode keeps everything in the browser.

PQC Assistant: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) with 12,000+ corpus chunks from 22+ data sources, powered by Gemini 2.5 Flash. Requires user-provided Google API key (BYOK). Three capabilities: Grounded Answers, Deep Linking, PQC Domain Expertise.

License: GPL-3.0 (GNU General Public License v3.0).

Creator & Maintainer: Eric Amador. Eric Amador is the sole developer and maintainer of PQC Today (pqctoday.com). LinkedIn profile: https://www.linkedin.com/in/eric-amador-971850a/. To connect with Eric or learn more about his background, visit the About page (/about) or his LinkedIn profile. AI tools acknowledged: Google Antigravity, ChatGPT, Claude AI, Perplexity, Gemini Pro.

chunks.title: PQC Today — Transparency, Disclaimer & Site Status
chunks.content:
PQC Today — Transparency & Disclaimer (Site Status)

PQC Today is a work in progress (WIP). It is a community-driven educational platform built to help professionals understand and prepare for the post-quantum cryptography transition.

Endorsement status: As of now, PQC Today has NOT received endorsement from any of the organizations, standards bodies, or government agencies referenced in its content (such as NIST, ETSI, IETF, BSI, ANSSI, ISO/IEC, or Common Criteria). However, we are actively working toward obtaining endorsement and recognition from these organizations. We are engaging with authoritative bodies and domain experts to cross-validate content and build credibility. Endorsement is a goal we are pursuing, not something we claim today.

Content validation process: All content on PQC Today goes through a multi-layer validation process. We use automated cross-checking with multiple AI platforms to verify accuracy and consistency across data sources, combined with manual review by the maintainer. We are also actively seeking peer review support from domain experts and authoritative organizations, but formal peer review is not yet in place. This means the content has been carefully checked but has not yet undergone independent expert validation.

Key disclaimers:
- All information is sourced from publicly available resources on the internet.
- Content is validated through automated AI-assisted cross-checking and manual review, but formal peer review is not yet in place.
- The content may still contain inaccuracies despite our best efforts.
- We are actively seeking peer reviewers and domain experts to further strengthen content quality.
- Industry leaders featured on this platform are included only with their written consent.

If you represent a cited organization, are a domain expert, or simply want to help improve the accuracy of this platform, you can get involved via GitHub Discussions or by contacting Eric Amador on LinkedIn.

The platform is under active development. New features, data sources, and learning modules are added regularly. Check the Changelog (/changelog) for the latest updates.

If someone asks "is this endorsed?", "who endorses this?", "is this endorsed by NIST?", "is this official?" — the answer is: PQC Today is not yet endorsed by any referenced organization, but we are actively working to obtain endorsement from standards bodies and government agencies. If someone asks "what is the status of this site?", "is this site finished?", "is this a beta?", "is this work in progress?", "is the data accurate?", or "can I trust this site?" — direct them to the Transparency & Disclaimer section on the About page (/about#transparency). The site is a work in progress, community-driven, and actively pursuing endorsement. If someone asks "how is the content validated?", "how do you verify accuracy?", "is this peer reviewed?", "how do you check the data?", or "what is your validation process?" — explain that we use automated cross-checking with multiple AI platforms plus manual review, and that we are seeking peer review support but it is not yet in place.

chunks.content:
