chunks.title: Protocol Support Matrix: SSH
chunks.content:
Protocol: SSH
Secure Shell — transport-layer security for remote login and tunneling.
PQC Standardization Status:
Pure KEM: draft (individual-draft)
  Stage note: Internet-Draft
  Note: ML-KEM-1024 required by CNSA 2.0 SSH profile from 2027 (Independent Submission track).
Hybrid KEM: rfc (rfc-published)
  Stage note: RFC 9941 (sntrup761 hybrid) published 2026-04; the ML-KEM hybrid key exchange (draft-ietf-sshm-mlkem-hybrid-kex) was published as RFC 10042 (Informational) in August 2026.
Pure Signature: draft (individual-draft)
  Stage note: Internet-Drafts (individual)
Hybrid Signature: draft (wg-document)
  Stage note: Verified live 2026-09-01: the individual submission was adopted by the SSHM working group and replaced by draft-ietf-sshm-composite-sigs (WG document, IESG state "I-D Exists"). Was individual-draft.
  Note: Composite ML-DSA+Ed25519 host-key authentication track; the CNSA 2.0 SSH profile (Independent Submission) also touches composite-sig host-key semantics. OpenSSH 10.4 (2026-07-06) shipped the first implementation — experimental, opt-in support for mldsa44-ed25519 host keys and user auth (ssh-keygen -t mldsa44-ed25519; not enabled by default).

Documents: RFC-4253, RFC-9941, RFC-10042, draft-ietf-sshm-mlkem-hybrid-kex-10, draft-harrison-sshm-mlkem, draft-sfluhrer-ssh-mldsa, draft-josefsson-ssh-sphincs, draft-ietf-sshm-composite-sigs, draft-becker-cnsa2-ssh-profile-05
OSS Libraries: OpenSSH
Live Deployments:
  • OpenSSH: mlkem768x25519-sha256 default key exchange since OpenSSH 10.0 (added in 9.9); 10.1+ warns on non-PQ KEX (since 2025-04)
  • GitHub SSH: sntrup761x25519-sha512 on github.com and GHEC (from 2025-09-17); US data-residency region excluded for FIPS compliance (since 2025-09)
  • AWS Transfer Family: ML-KEM SSH KEX policies for SFTP (TransferSecurityPolicy-2025-03) (since 2025-05)
Recommended for production PQC today. RFC 9941 published (April 2026) standardizes sntrup761x25519 — the hybrid GitHub SSH runs; mlkem768x25519 ships by default in OpenSSH 10.0 and is offered by AWS Transfer Family.

chunks.title: Protocol Support Matrix: TLS 1.2
chunks.content:
Protocol: TLS 1.2
Legacy transport-layer security — no PQC standardization path.
PQC Standardization Status:
Pure KEM: na (none)
  Stage note: No PQC track for TLS 1.2
  Note: IETF TLS WG has scoped all PQC work to TLS 1.3 only.
Hybrid KEM: na (none)
  Stage note: No PQC track for TLS 1.2
  Note: No IETF draft proposes hybrid PQC for TLS 1.2.
Pure Signature: na (none)
  Stage note: No PQC track for TLS 1.2
  Note: No PQC signature support planned for TLS 1.2.
Hybrid Signature: na (none)
  Stage note: No PQC track for TLS 1.2
  Note: No PQC signature support planned for TLS 1.2.

Documents: RFC-5246, RFC-9325
OSS Libraries: OpenSSL, BoringSSL
No live deployments: By design — the IETF TLS WG scoped all PQC work to TLS 1.3 only (TLS 1.2 BCP recommends migrating off TLS 1.2). Operators must migrate to TLS 1.3 to obtain any PQ posture; no path exists to retrofit PQ key exchange or signatures into TLS 1.2 transport.
Inherited by: DTLS 1.2, FIDO

chunks.title: Protocol Support Matrix: TLS 1.3
chunks.content:
Protocol: TLS 1.3
Modern transport-layer security with hybrid + pure PQC key exchange and PQ signatures.
PQC Standardization Status:
Pure KEM: draft (rfc-editor-queue)
  Stage note: Re-checked 2026-10-17: draft-ietf-tls-mlkem-11 is in the RFC Editor queue (IESG approval announced after the 2026-09-03 telechat).
Hybrid KEM: rfc (rfc-published)
  Stage note: Published as RFC 10024 on 2026-08-10 — revision -05 of the hybrid ECDHE-MLKEM draft is the revision that became the RFC, so the earlier "RFC Editor queue" note is superseded rather than contradicted. Verified against the datatracker: the draft carries state slug `rfc` and IESG state `pub`, and relateddocument records `became_rfc -> rfc10024`.
  Note: X25519MLKEM768 hybrid group (IANA codepoint 4588) — deployed in production since 2024, and standards-track as of 2026-08-10.
Pure Signature: draft (rfc-editor-queue)
  Stage note: Re-checked 2026-10-17: draft-ietf-tls-mldsa-06 is in the RFC Editor queue (approved by the IESG at the 2026-07-02 telechat).
Hybrid Signature: draft (wg-document)
  Stage note: The TLS WG adopted draft-ietf-tls-composite-mldsa on 2026-10-23. The X.509-layer draft-ietf-lamps-pq-composite-sigs dependency has IESG state "RFC Ed Queue".
  Note: Three approaches to composite/hybrid signatures for TLS 1.3 are documented: dual-certificate negotiation remains an individual Internet-Draft, the TLS WG has adopted composite ML-DSA for the handshake, and the LAMPS composite-signature work supplies the X.509-layer construction that TLS profiles.

Documents: RFC-9846, RFC 10024, draft-ietf-tls-mlkem-11, draft-ietf-tls-mldsa-06, RFC-9954-Hybrid-Key-Exchange-in-TLS-1-3, draft-yusef-tls-pqt-dual-certs
OSS Libraries: OpenSSL 3.5.0, AWS-LC, BoringSSL, rustls, oqs-provider, JEP 527: Post-Quantum Hybrid Key Exchange for TLS 1.3
Live Deployments:
  • Cloudflare: X25519MLKEM768 default at the edge for all TLS 1.3 connections (since 2024-10)
  • Google Chrome: X25519MLKEM768 default for TLS 1.3 and QUIC in Chrome 131 (Chrome 124, Apr 2024, shipped the earlier X25519Kyber768Draft00 pre-standard group, not ML-KEM) (since 2024-11)
  • AWS: ML-KEM hybrid TLS supported in AWS KMS, ACM, and Secrets Manager; Kyber support runs alongside ML-KEM, with removal slated for 2026 (since 2025-04)
  • AWS Application/Network Load Balancer: Opt-in PQ-TLS security policies (SecP256r1MLKEM768, SecP384r1MLKEM1024, X25519MLKEM768) for ALB/NLB listeners — the actual internet-facing TLS termination products, distinct from the KMS/ACM/Secrets Manager entry above (since 2025-11)
  • Akamai: Hybrid ML-KEM + X25519 key exchange for browser-to-edge connections on Ion / Dynamic Site Accelerator (Enhanced TLS), limited availability opt-in (since 2025-09)
  • Fastly: ML-KEM post-quantum key exchange rolling out across the global CDN fleet (since 2025-04)
  • Apple iOS / macOS: X25519MLKEM768 advertised in TLS 1.3 from iOS 26 / macOS 26 (shipped 2025-09-15) (since 2025-09)
  • Microsoft (Windows / Server / .NET): SymCrypt ships ML-KEM + ML-DSA GA via CNG/certificate APIs on Windows 11 (24H2/25H2), Windows Server 2025, and .NET 10; Azure service-level PQC (e.g. Key Vault) is rolling out separately through 2026–27, not GA alongside this release (since 2025-11)
  • OpenSSL 3.5+: Default TLS keyshares offer X25519MLKEM768 (3.5 LTS) (since 2025-04)
  • F5 BIG-IP: X25519_ML-KEM-768 hybrid in TLS 1.3 (named group requires TMOS 17.5.1+; 17.5.0 shipped an earlier Kyber hybrid) (since 2025)
  • Symantec SWG (Broadcom): X25519MLKEM768 hybrid KEX as first-to-market SWG PQ capability (since 2025)
  • Mozilla Firefox: mlkem768x25519 (X25519MLKEM768) default for TLS 1.3 HTTPS since Firefox 132 (via NSS 3.105) (since 2024-10)
  • Google Android: Android 17 adds ML-DSA to Keystore and Verified Boot; announced/beta Mar 2026, stable rollout (Pixel) 2026-06-16 (since 2026-06)
Recommended for production PQC today. X25519MLKEM768 hybrid group in production at Cloudflare, Google, and AWS; specified in RFC 10024 (August 2026).
Inherited by: DTLS 1.3, FIDO 2, MACsec, QUIC

chunks.title: Protocol Support Matrix: X.509
chunks.content:
Protocol: X.509
PKI certificate format — algorithm OIDs for ML-DSA / ML-KEM / SLH-DSA + composite (hybrid) variants.
PQC Standardization Status:
Pure KEM: rfc (rfc-published)
  Stage note: RFC 9935 published 2026-03
  Note: Constraint: KEM certs are encryption-only — cannot self-sign, must be issued under a signature cert. A LAMPS working-group draft defines FrodoKEM for X.509, and FrodoKEM is not a NIST-standardized algorithm.
Hybrid KEM: draft (rfc-editor-queue)
  Stage note: RFC Editor queue: the IESG approved draft-ietf-lamps-pq-composite-kem; the datatracker shows IESG state "RFC Ed Queue" (changed 2026-10-12), current revision -23 (2026-10-14). Not yet published as an RFC. Datatracker history checked 2026-10-30.
  Note: Composite mode pairs ML-KEM with RSA-OAEP / ECDH / X25519 / X448 classical KEMs.
Pure Signature: rfc (rfc-published)
  Stage note: RFC 9909 (SLH-DSA, Dec 2025) + RFC 9881 (ML-DSA, Oct 2025)
Hybrid Signature: draft (rfc-editor-queue)
  Stage note: RFC Ed Queue (EDIT) — draft-ietf-lamps-pq-composite-sigs-19
  Note: Composite mode pairs ML-DSA with ECDSA / RSA / Ed25519 / EdDSA classical signatures.

Documents: RFC-5280, RFC-9881, RFC-9935, RFC-9909, RFC-9763, RFC-9802, RFC-9925, draft-ietf-lamps-pq-composite-sigs-19, draft-ietf-lamps-pq-composite-kem-23, draft-ietf-lamps-certdiscovery-03, draft-ietf-lamps-fn-dsa-certificates-00, draft-ietf-lamps-one-signature-certs-02
OSS Libraries: OpenSSL 3.5.0, Bouncy Castle Java, oqs-provider, AWS-LC
Live Deployments:
  • X9 Financial PKI (operated by DigiCert): Managed PKI for financial services; offers legacy + PQC algorithms for transition (since 2025-02)
  • AWS Private CA: ML-DSA X.509 certificate issuance for quantum-resistant code signing roots of trust (since 2025)
  • Microsoft AD CS: ML-DSA certificate issuance GA on Windows Server 2025 Active Directory Certificate Services (since 2026-05)
  • Cloudflare: Accepts ML-DSA (FIPS 204) origin certificates via Authenticated Origin Pulls + Custom Origin Trust Store (since 2026-06)
Inherited by: UEFI

chunks.title: Protocol Support Matrix: S/MIME (CMS)
chunks.content:
Protocol: S/MIME (CMS)
Cryptographic Message Syntax for signed/encrypted email and S/MIME messages.
PQC Standardization Status:
Pure KEM: rfc (rfc-published)
  Stage note: RFC 9936 published 2026-03
  Note: A LAMPS working-group draft defines FrodoKEM for CMS, and FrodoKEM is not a NIST-standardized algorithm.
Hybrid KEM: draft (rfc-editor-queue)
  Stage note: Re-checked 2026-10-17: draft-ietf-lamps-cms-composite-kem-04 is in the RFC Editor queue, after IETF Last Call (closed 2026-08-18) and IESG review. This draft defines the CMS KEMRecipientInfo composite-ML-KEM structure S/MIME itself uses, not a borrowed dependency.
  Note: Uses the CMS KEMRecipientInfo structure; pairs ML-KEM with RSA-OAEP / ECDH / X25519 / X448 classical KEMs.
Pure Signature: rfc (rfc-published)
  Stage note: RFC 9882 (ML-DSA) published 2025-10; FN-DSA-in-CMS still in early WG draft (draft-ietf-lamps-cms-fn-dsa-00, 2026-05)
Hybrid Signature: draft (rfc-editor-queue)
  Stage note: IETF Last Call completed (directorate reviews Apr 2026) — now in RFC Editor queue (draft-05)
  Note: Composite ML-DSA SignerInfo construction mirrors the X.509 composite-sigs row.

Documents: RFC-8551, RFC-5652, RFC-9936, RFC-9882, RFC-9814, RFC-9629, draft-ietf-lamps-cms-composite-kem-04, draft-ietf-lamps-cms-composite-sigs-05, draft-becker-cnsa2-smime-profile-05
OSS Libraries: Bouncy Castle Java, NSS (Mozilla), OpenSSL 3.5.0
No live deployments: S/MIME PQ standards are very fresh (ML-DSA Oct 2025, SLH-DSA Jul 2025, ML-KEM Mar 2026) — typical standards-to-ship gap is 12–24 months. The quantum-safe consumer-email market migrated to OpenPGP (Proton Mail) and proprietary protocols (Tuta / TutaCrypt) rather than S/MIME; mainstream providers (Gmail / Outlook / Apple Mail) rely on TLS-in-transit + at-rest encryption and do not drive S/MIME at all. The procurement-cycle slots that will force S/MIME PQ deployment — the CNSA 2.0 S/MIME profile (draft-becker-cnsa2-smime-profile-05, still draft) and X9 Financial PKI consumers — have not yet shipped a product. Building blocks (OpenSSL 3.5 `cms`, Bouncy Castle 1.79+ CMS API) exist and IETF Hackathon runs cross-vendor interop tests, but no end-user product deployment.

chunks.title: Protocol Support Matrix: COSE
chunks.content:
Protocol: COSE
CBOR Object Signing and Encryption — IoT-oriented peer to S/MIME; ML-DSA and FN-DSA algorithm identifiers in active drafts.
PQC Standardization Status:
Pure KEM: draft (wg-document)
  Stage note: Two COSE WG documents cover distinct uses: draft-ietf-cose-hpke-pq-pqt registers PQ and PQ/T algorithms for HPKE, while draft-ietf-cose-pqc-kem defines direct ML-KEM use in COSE.
Hybrid KEM: draft (wg-document)
  Stage note: Corrected 2026-09-03, same fix as pure KEM: draft-ietf-cose-hpke has no PQ registrations, draft-ietf-jose-hpke-pq-pqt is JOSE-only. draft-ietf-cose-hpke-pq-pqt is the real COSE-specific document, at 'I-D Exists' — pre-WG-Last-Call, so wg-document.
  Note: Same HPKE construction covers both pure and hybrid KEM modes.
Pure Signature: rfc (rfc-published)
  Stage note: RFC 9964 published May 2026 — ML-DSA-44/65/87; FN-DSA (draft-ietf-cose-falcon) still WG-doc
Hybrid Signature: draft (wg-document)
  Stage note: WG document (datatracker 2026-02-27) — same status as the JOSE row; ENISA "Hybridization Standardisation Status" (30 Apr 2026) independently confirms WG Draft
  Note: Composite signatures are specified at the JOSE layer — see JOSE row.

Documents: RFC-9052, RFC-9053, RFC-9964, draft-ietf-cose-falcon-04, draft-ietf-cose-hpke-27, draft-ietf-jose-hpke-pq-pqt-01
OSS Libraries: Bouncy Castle Java
No live deployments: COSE PQ standards are still in WG draft and the consumer/IoT products that would consume COSE-PQ signatures (passkeys / WebAuthn / constrained-device firmware) are themselves pre-deployment. IANA registered COSE alg IDs for ML-DSA in April 2025, but no commercial COSE-PQ product has shipped.

chunks.title: Protocol Support Matrix: EDHOC (lightweight authenticated key exchange)
chunks.content:
Protocol: EDHOC (lightweight authenticated key exchange)
Ephemeral Diffie-Hellman Over COSE (EDHOC) is a compact authenticated key-exchange protocol for constrained environments; the IETF LAKE working group is adding post-quantum cipher suites and KEM-based authentication.
PQC Standardization Status:
Pure KEM: draft (wg-document)
  Stage note: The LAKE WG documents define ML-KEM for ephemeral key exchange and a signature-free KEM-based authentication method.
  Note: ML-KEM cipher suites provide pure post-quantum key exchange; the KEM-authentication method can use ML-KEM for both key exchange and authentication.
Hybrid KEM: none (none)
  Stage note: PQ/T hybrid KEM registrations are left for future work
  Note: The current LAKE WG documents register pure ML-KEM cipher suites, not a PQ/T hybrid KEM suite.
Pure Signature: draft (wg-document)
  Stage note: The LAKE WG cipher-suite document registers ML-DSA authentication
  Note: The quantum-resistant cipher suites use ML-DSA-44 or ML-DSA-87 for digital signatures.
Hybrid Signature: none (none)
  Stage note: PQ/T hybrid signature registrations are left for future work
  Note: The current LAKE WG documents register pure ML-DSA cipher suites, not a PQ/T hybrid signature suite.

Documents: RFC-9528, draft-ietf-lake-pqsuites-01, draft-ietf-lake-authkem-edhoc-01
No live deployments: The post-quantum mechanisms are active LAKE working-group documents and are not yet published RFCs.

chunks.title: Protocol Support Matrix: JOSE
chunks.content:
Protocol: JOSE
JSON Object Signing and Encryption (JWS/JWE/JWT) — ML-DSA in JWS is RFC 9964; composite signatures, SLH-DSA and HPKE-based ML-KEM encryption for JWE are active drafts.
PQC Standardization Status:
Pure KEM: draft (wg-document)
  Stage note: Corrected 2026-10-01: pure ML-KEM for JWE is registered by draft-ietf-jose-hpke-pq-pqt-01 ('I-D Exists', pre-WG-Last-Call) on top of draft-ietf-jose-hpke-encrypt-22 (RFC Editor queue). The previously cited JOSE PQ-KEM draft (jose-pqc-kem) became COSE-only in its -06 revision (2026-07-06).
  Note: Same HPKE construction covers both pure and hybrid KEM modes.
Hybrid KEM: draft (wg-document)
  Stage note: draft-ietf-jose-hpke-encrypt is in the RFC Editor queue (blocked on a normative reference, checked 2026-10-01), but it's algorithm-agnostic HPKE-JOSE plumbing — it doesn't register ML-KEM identifiers. draft-ietf-jose-hpke-pq-pqt is the document that actually does, and it remains at 'I-D Exists' — pre-WG-Last-Call. Real PQC support needs both documents, so this cell tracks the lagging, algorithm-defining one.
  Note: Same HPKE construction covers both pure and hybrid KEM modes.
Pure Signature: rfc (rfc-published)
  Stage note: RFC 9964 published May 2026 — ML-DSA-44/65/87 for JWS. SLH-DSA (SHA2-128s, SHAKE-128s) is still a draft: draft-ietf-cose-sphincs-plus-10, AD Evaluation.
Hybrid Signature: draft (wg-document)
  Stage note: WG document, 'I-D Exists' — draft-04 (2026-09-11), checked 2026-10-01

Documents: RFC-7515, RFC-7516, RFC-7519, RFC-9964, draft-ietf-jose-pq-composite-sigs-06, draft-ietf-jose-hpke-encrypt-22, draft-ietf-jose-hpke-pq-pqt-01, draft-ietf-cose-sphincs-plus-10
OSS Libraries: Nimbus JOSE+JWT, Bouncy Castle Java, jose4j, go-jose v4, PyJWT
Live Deployments:
  • AWS KMS: ML-DSA signing GA (June 2025), with an AWS Security Blog walkthrough that signs and verifies a JWT (alg ML-DSA-65) through KMS (since 2025-06)

chunks.title: Protocol Support Matrix: EST / CMP
chunks.content:
Protocol: EST / CMP
PKI enrollment protocols — RFC 7030 (EST) and RFC 9810 (CMP, KEM update) carry composite ML-DSA/ML-KEM requests for PQ cert issuance.
PQC Standardization Status:
Pure KEM: rfc (rfc-published)
  Stage note: RFC 9810 (CMP KEM support, Jul 2025) + RFC 9935 (X.509 ML-KEM OIDs, Mar 2026)
  Note: ML-KEM X.509 OIDs apply from the X.509 row; CMP adds KEM key-transport semantics on top.
Hybrid KEM: draft (rfc-editor-queue)
  Stage note: Inherits draft-ietf-lamps-pq-composite-kem (see X.509 row): IESG state "RFC Ed Queue" since 2026-10-12, current revision -23 (2026-10-14); not yet published as an RFC. Datatracker history checked 2026-10-30.
  Note: Composite enrollment uses PKCS#10 / CMP wrappers — see X.509 row for the composite KEM construction.
Pure Signature: rfc (rfc-published)
  Stage note: RFC 7030 (EST, 2013) + RFC 9881 (X.509 ML-DSA OIDs, Oct 2025)
  Note: ML-DSA enrollment uses X.509 ML-DSA OIDs (see X.509 row); CSR and CMP response flows defined.
Hybrid Signature: draft (rfc-editor-queue)
  Stage note: Inherited from X.509 row — draft-ietf-lamps-pq-composite-sigs-19 in RFC Editor queue
  Note: Composite-sig CSR / issuance flows wrap the X.509 composite-sigs construction — see X.509 row.

Documents: RFC-7030, RFC-9810, draft-ietf-lamps-pq-composite-kem-19, draft-ietf-lamps-pq-composite-sigs-19
OSS Libraries: Bouncy Castle Java, OpenSSL 3.5.0, SignServer, smallstep step-ca
Live Deployments:
  • EJBCA (Keyfactor): ML-DSA via CMP (RA Verified POP) + ML-KEM via CMP (encrCert POP) cert enrollment since EJBCA 9.1 (since 2024)

chunks.title: Protocol Support Matrix: Kerberos
chunks.content:
Protocol: Kerberos
Network authentication protocol (AS/TGS exchanges) — the core protocol is symmetric-key by design and already quantum-safe by construction. PKINIT, the optional public-key preauthentication extension, is the only asymmetric-crypto surface and has no chartered PQC work — only individual (non-WG) drafts.
PQC Standardization Status:
Pure KEM: draft (individual-draft)
  Stage note: The KITTEN working group has issued a call for adoption for draft-bokovoy-kitten-pkinit-pqc; it was not yet adopted as of the page update on 2026-10-16
  Note: Core Kerberos (AS-REQ/AS-REP/TGS-REQ/TGS-REP without PKINIT) uses only symmetric long-term/session keys (RFC 3961 framework) — no KEM applies, and NIST/academic consensus treats symmetric crypto as already quantum-resistant (Grover gives only a quadratic speedup, already covered by AES-256/SHA-384+). PKINIT's key establishment is classical Diffie-Hellman with no PQC-safe path via existing agility mechanisms — this draft adds a new KDCKEMInfo structure carrying ML-KEM (RFC 9935 X.509 OIDs) alongside the existing DH fields. Red Hat is prototyping this under the EU-funded QARC consortium (2026–2028) against MIT krb5 + FreeIPA; no public code yet.
Hybrid KEM: draft (individual-draft)
  Stage note: The KITTEN working group has issued a call for adoption for draft-bokovoy-kitten-pkinit-pqc; it was not yet adopted as of the page update on 2026-10-16 and remains at IESG state 'I-D Exists'.
  Note: Same draft as Pure KEM; hybrid mode composes with draft-ietf-lamps-pq-composite-kem, approved at the X.509 layer and in the RFC Editor queue since 2026-10-12 (see X.509 row). The Kerberos-side mechanism itself remains an individual draft.
Pure Signature: experimental
  Note: PKINIT already has signature/digest algorithm agility (RFC 8636, 2019), so a KDC/client could in principle present ML-DSA certificates (RFC 9881 X.509 OIDs, RFC 9882 CMS) without a new PKINIT-specific spec — but no implementation has been confirmed to do this. Microsoft AD CS (Windows Server 2025) can issue ML-DSA certificates generally (GA, May 2026) but this is NOT confirmed to be wired into Kerberos/PKINIT specifically.
Hybrid Signature: experimental (individual-draft)
  Stage note: Individual draft active (draft-bokovoy-kitten-pkinit-pqc, datatracker 2026-07-18)
  Note: Same agility-based path as Pure Signature; draft-bokovoy-kitten-pkinit-pqc optionally mentions composite ML-DSA per the LAMPS composite-sigs draft, but this is unadopted and unimplemented.

Documents: RFC-4120, RFC-4556, RFC-8636, RFC-3961, draft-bokovoy-kitten-pkinit-pqc-02
No live deployments: No shipping implementation exists. MIT krb5 has no public PQC roadmap item or commit. Red Hat is prototyping PKINIT+ML-KEM under the EU Horizon-funded QARC consortium (2026–2028, targeting MIT krb5 + FreeIPA) — the same engineers behind the one individual IETF draft above — but no public code has landed yet. Microsoft has GA'd general ML-DSA certificate issuance (AD CS, Windows Server 2025) and lists "Kerberos" in one generic future-roadmap sentence, but has made no concrete, verified announcement of PQC support inside the Kerberos/PKINIT authentication path itself.

chunks.title: Protocol Support Matrix: 5G SUCI (3GPP)
chunks.content:
Protocol: 5G SUCI (3GPP)
3GPP 5G Subscription Concealed Identifier — protects the subscriber IMSI/SUPI in transit. No 3GPP TS defines a PQC concealment profile yet; the Rel-20 study TR 33.703 on transitioning to PQC covers 3GPP-specific protocols including the SUCI calculation. ML-KEM-based SUCI schemes exist so far only as vendor research.
PQC Standardization Status:
Pure KEM: experimental (identified)
  Note: No 3GPP TS defines a PQC SUCI concealment profile yet. The PCG-approved Release 20 work item "Post-quantum Cryptography Migration for SUCI" started 2026-09-08, while TR 33.703 has been under change control since 2026-06-17.
Hybrid KEM: experimental (identified)
  Note: No 3GPP TS defines a hybrid SUCI construction. The PCG-approved Release 20 work item "Post-quantum Cryptography Migration for SUCI" started 2026-09-08, while TR 33.703 has been under change control since 2026-06-17.
Pure Signature: na
  Note: SUCI concealment is a KEM-based privacy mechanism; no signatures.
Hybrid Signature: na
  Note: SUCI concealment is a KEM-based privacy mechanism; no signatures.

Documents: 3GPP-TS-33.501, 3GPP-TR-33.703, 3GPP-TR-33.938
Live Deployments:
  • SK Telecom + Thales: Crystals-Kyber (ML-KEM) lab trial on a 5G SA network with 5G SIM cards to protect subscriber identity — a trial, not a commercial deployment (since 2023-12)

chunks.title: Protocol Support Matrix: OpenPGP
chunks.content:
Protocol: OpenPGP
OpenPGP message format — composite ML-KEM+X25519/X448 encryption and ML-DSA+Ed25519/Ed448 signatures, plus standalone SLH-DSA.
PQC Standardization Status:
Pure KEM: experimental (experimental)
  Stage note: No pure ML-KEM track; OpenPGP-PQC ships composite only
  Note: OpenPGP-PQC ships composite KEM only; pure ML-KEM mode is chartered but not yet specified.
Hybrid KEM: rfc (rfc-published)
  Stage note: RFC 9980 published Jun 2026 (formerly the OpenPGP-PQC draft) — covers Hybrid KEM + Pure/Hybrid Sig
  Note: Composite mode pairs ML-KEM-768 with X25519 (MUST) and ML-KEM-1024 with X448 (SHOULD). RFC 9980 covers Pure Sig and Hybrid Sig in the same document; NIST and Brainpool curve composites are in draft-ietf-openpgp-nist-bp-comp.
Pure Signature: rfc (rfc-published)
  Stage note: RFC 9980 published Jun 2026 — same document as Hybrid KEM
Hybrid Signature: rfc (rfc-published)
  Stage note: RFC 9980 published Jun 2026 — same document as Hybrid KEM
  Note: Composite mode pairs ML-DSA-65 with Ed25519 (MUST) and ML-DSA-87 with Ed448 (SHOULD).

Documents: RFC-9580, RFC-9980, draft-ietf-openpgp-nist-bp-comp-05, draft-ietf-openpgp-persistent-symmetric-keys-04
OSS Libraries: GnuPG, Sequoia-PGP PQC, OpenPGP.js
Live Deployments:
  • Proton Mail: Hybrid ML-KEM (OpenPGP v6) encryption available to all plans incl. free — opt-in, gradual rollout, applies to new messages only (since 2026-05)

chunks.title: Protocol Support Matrix: IKE / IPsec
chunks.content:
Protocol: IKE / IPsec
Internet Key Exchange v2 and IPsec — ML-KEM as additional key exchange and ML-DSA / SLH-DSA for authentication.
PQC Standardization Status:
Pure KEM: draft (rfc-editor-queue)
  Stage note: DISCUSS cleared after the 2026-07-02 telechat — now in RFC Editor queue (draft-09); same draft covers Pure + Hybrid KEM
  Note: IKEv2 multi-KE framework (RFC 9370) carries either pure or hybrid ML-KEM. There is NO RFC for IKEv2 hybrid KEM yet — both modes ride the same draft. Known limit (draft-09 §2.1): pure ML-KEM must travel in IKE_SA_INIT, which IKEv2 fragmentation cannot split, so over UDP only ML-KEM-512 is unconditionally allowed. ML-KEM-768/1024 (CNSA 2.0) need a guaranteed sufficient PMTU or IKE over TCP, else IP fragmentation. The hybrid route (Appendix A) moves ML-KEM to IKE_INTERMEDIATE to avoid this.
Hybrid KEM: draft (rfc-editor-queue)
  Stage note: REVERTED 2026-07-27: a hand-verified apply incorrectly set this to rfc-published on the strength of RFC 9370 alone — but RFC 9370 is the shared multi-KE enabler framework both dimensions cite, not the hybrid-KEM-specific mechanism. See the note below, which already documented this exact mistake before this revert.
  Note: Same draft as Pure KEM. No standalone RFC for hybrid KEM in IKEv2 (corrects an earlier mis-encoding to "rfc"). RFC 9370 multi-KE framework + draft-ietf-ipsecme-ikev2-mlkem together define the hybrid binding; the binding draft itself is still in the RFC Editor queue, matching Pure KEM. An IPSECME working-group draft defines FrodoKEM key exchange for IKEv2, and FrodoKEM is not a NIST-standardized algorithm.
Pure Signature: draft (rfc-editor-queue)
  Stage note: Verified live 2026-09-01: draft-ietf-ipsecme-ikev2-pqc-auth has cleared IESG evaluation and is now in the RFC Editor queue, "Awaiting Editor Assignment" (revision -12, last updated 2026-08-31; OPSDIR review of -10 on 2026-08-04, SECDIR review of -10 on 2026-07-26, both clean). Supersedes the 2026-08-22 reading of "Submitted to IESG for Publication".
Hybrid Signature: draft (wg-document)
  Stage note: draft-ietf-ipsecme-pq-hybrid-auth-00 is an IPSECME working-group document, published 2026-10-29
  Note: The IPSECME working-group document specifies composite-signature authentication for IKEv2; an earlier individual submission by overlapping authors remains listed for context.

Documents: RFC-7296, RFC-8784, RFC-9370, RFC-9867, RFC-9242, draft-ietf-ipsecme-ikev2-mlkem-09, draft-ietf-ipsecme-ikev2-pqc-auth-12, draft-hu-ipsecme-pqt-hybrid-auth
OSS Libraries: strongSwan, Libreswan
Live Deployments:
  • Cloudflare WARP: WARP client uses post-quantum hybrid key agreement (since 2024)
  • Cloudflare IPsec: PQ IPsec GA at Cloudflare; interop with Cisco / Fortinet (since 2026)
  • ExpressVPN Lightway: Lightway upgraded to ML-KEM (Level 5) via wolfSSL (since 2025-01)
  • Cisco Secure Firewall: Hybrid IKEv2 (IKE_INTERMEDIATE + multi-KE RFCs) live on ASA 9.19+; ML-KEM support in FTD 10.5 / ASA 9.25 is ROADMAP, targeted for late 2026 — not yet shipped (since 2024)
  • Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS: PQC Site-to-Site VPN with hybrid IKEv2; PAN-OS 11.2 uses pre-standard KEMs (Kyber/BIKE/FrodoKEM/HQC) — ML-KEM itself arrived only in PAN-OS 12.1+ (since 2025)

chunks.title: Protocol Support Matrix: WireGuard
chunks.content:
Protocol: WireGuard
Modern kernel-level VPN tunnel protocol — no IETF/formal PQC standardization track. PQ protection is added by injecting a post-quantum KEM-derived secret into the existing pre-shared-key (PSK) mechanism (e.g. the Rosenpass protocol), not by changing the wire protocol itself.
PQC Standardization Status:
Pure KEM: na
  Note: WireGuard's Noise-based handshake has no pure-PQ-only mode — PQ protection rides on the existing PSK mechanism (see Hybrid KEM).
Hybrid KEM: experimental
  Stage note: Vendor/community technique (Rosenpass whitepaper, formally verified with ProVerif) — not an IETF or WireGuard-project standard
  Note: Rosenpass runs a separate handshake using Classic McEliece-460896 (static keys) and round-3 Kyber-512 (ephemeral keys), not FIPS 203 ML-KEM, and injects the combined shared secret into WireGuard's existing pre-shared-key (PSK) slot — an out-of-band combiner, not a change to the WireGuard wire protocol. Several VPN vendors ship equivalent WireGuard + ML-KEM hybrid combiners.
Pure Signature: na
  Note: WireGuard authenticates peers with static Curve25519 keys, not certificates or signatures — no PQ signature dimension applies.
Hybrid Signature: na
  Note: Same as Pure Signature — WireGuard has no signature dimension to hybridize.

Documents: Rosenpass-Protocol
OSS Libraries: WireGuard, wireguard-go, Rosenpass
Live Deployments:
  • Mullvad VPN: Quantum-resistant WireGuard default on all desktop platforms — PQ KEM-negotiated PSK (Rosenpass-style) injected into the WireGuard handshake (since 2025-01)

chunks.title: Protocol Support Matrix: MLS
chunks.content:
Protocol: MLS
Messaging Layer Security — group messaging with forward-secure ratcheting; PQ cipher suites and combiners in WG Last Call.
PQC Standardization Status:
Pure KEM: draft (wg-last-call)
  Stage note: Waiting for WG Chair Go-Ahead (draft-05, 2026-07-02); revised I-D needed after WGLC feedback. Single draft covers all 4 cases
Hybrid KEM: draft (wg-last-call)
  Stage note: Waiting for WG Chair Go-Ahead (draft-05, 2026-07-02); revised I-D needed after WGLC feedback; same draft as Pure KEM
  Note: Combiner seeds PQ guarantees into the traditional ciphersuite via the exporter secret.
Pure Signature: draft (wg-last-call)
  Stage note: Waiting for WG Chair Go-Ahead (draft-05, 2026-07-02); revised I-D needed after WGLC feedback; same draft as Pure KEM
  Note: Cipher suites bundle ML-DSA with the PQ KEM as a paired choice.
Hybrid Signature: draft (wg-last-call)
  Stage note: Waiting for WG Chair Go-Ahead (draft-05, 2026-07-02); revised I-D needed after WGLC feedback; same draft as Pure KEM
  Note: Hybrid sig path is via session combination; cert-layer composite-sigs lives in the X.509 row.

Documents: RFC-9420, draft-ietf-mls-pq-ciphersuites-06, draft-ietf-mls-combiner-02, draft-ietf-mls-extensions-10
OSS Libraries: OpenMLS, mls-rs, mlspp
No live deployments: No product ships PQ-MLS (RFC 9420 + draft-ietf-mls-pq-ciphersuites) today — the draft is still awaiting WG Chair Go-Ahead after WG Last Call. Apple iMessage PQ3 and Signal’s PQXDH are genuine production PQ messaging deployments, but they are proprietary ratchet protocols, NOT MLS — see the Signal (PQXDH) row for that deployment; iMessage PQ3 has no dedicated row since it is Apple-internal and unpublished as a formal spec.

chunks.title: Protocol Support Matrix: TPM
chunks.content:
Protocol: TPM
Trusted Platform Module — TPM 2.0 Library v1.85 (PUBLISHED 2026-03-12) adds ML-DSA, ML-KEM, Labeled KEM, EdDSA.
PQC Standardization Status:
Pure KEM: rfc (rfc-published)
  Stage note: TPM 2.0 Library v1.85 (Mar 2026) adds ML-KEM as an OPTIONAL algorithm; PC Client Platform TPM Profile v1.07 (2026-03-23) makes it mandatory
  Note: TPM 2.0 Library v1.85 defines ML-KEM-512/768/1024 as an optional algorithm (TPMA_ML_PARAMETER_SET capability bits) — the Library spec itself contains no SHALL-support text. The requirement to support ML-KEM-768 or ML-KEM-1024 comes from PC Client Platform TPM Profile v1.07, which governs PC-class TPMs, not the Library spec.
Hybrid KEM: experimental (experimental)
  Stage note: Labeled-KEM construct, not a TCG-standardized hybrid
  Note: TPM 2.0 Labeled KEM abstraction can mix algorithms; not standardized as "hybrid".
Pure Signature: rfc (rfc-published)
  Stage note: TPM 2.0 Library v1.85 (Mar 2026) adds ML-DSA as an OPTIONAL algorithm; PC Client Platform TPM Profile v1.07 (2026-03-23) makes it mandatory
  Note: TPM 2.0 Library v1.85 defines ML-DSA-44/65/87 (incl. HashML-DSA) as optional — no SHALL-support text in the Library spec itself. The requirement to support ML-DSA-65 or ML-DSA-87 comes from PC Client Platform TPM Profile v1.07.
Hybrid Signature: experimental (experimental)
  Stage note: Composite sig not in TCG scope; experimental dual-key constructs only
  Note: TPM signatures are atomic per-key; TCG v1.85 does not standardize a hybrid signature mode. Experimental dual-key constructs sit outside the TCG profile.

Documents: TCG-TPM-2.0-Library-v1.85-Part3-Published, TCG-PC-Client-Platform-TPM-Profile-v1.07, TCG-EK-Credential-Profile-v2.7, TCG-TPM-2.0-Library-v1.85-Errata
OSS Libraries: libtpms, swtpm, pqctoday-tpm, wolfTPM PQC
Live Deployments:
  • wolfTPM: wolfTPM ships initial TPM 2.0 v1.85 PQ commands (ML-DSA + ML-KEM) (since 2026)

chunks.title: Protocol Support Matrix: DNSSEC
chunks.content:
Protocol: DNSSEC
DNS Security Extensions — sig-only protocol; PQ adoption blocked by signature size vs DNS MTU.
PQC Standardization Status:
Pure KEM: na (na)
  Stage note: DNSSEC is signature-only
  Note: DNSSEC is a signature-only protocol; no KEM dimension.
Hybrid KEM: na (na)
  Stage note: DNSSEC is signature-only
  Note: DNSSEC is a signature-only protocol; no KEM dimension.
Pure Signature: experimental (individual-draft)
  Stage note: Individual drafts active (draft-westerbaan-dnssec-mldsa, draft-fregly-dnsop-slh-dsa-mtl-dnssec, draft-sheth-pqc-dnssec-strategy) — still no WG-chartered work
  Note: IANA has assigned DNSSEC algorithm number 18 to ML-DSA-44 (draft-westerbaan-dnssec-mldsa). Constraint unchanged: an ML-DSA-44 signature alone is 2,420 bytes, and SLH-DSA runs 7.8–49.8 KB — both exceed the ~1232-byte DNS UDP limit, forcing TCP fallback. No IETF WG currently addresses the IP fragmentation issue.
Hybrid Signature: experimental (individual-draft)
  Stage note: Individual draft active (draft-sheth-pqc-dnssec-strategy) — still no WG-chartered work
  Note: Strategy draft enumerates candidates; no concrete hybrid mode. Same UDP fragmentation barrier as pure sig.

Documents: RFC-4034, RFC-9364, draft-fregly-dnsop-slh-dsa-mtl-dnssec-06, draft-sheth-pqc-dnssec-strategy-02, draft-westerbaan-dnssec-mldsa-04
OSS Libraries: CoreDNS PQC DNSSEC, PowerDNS PQC DNSSEC, ISC BIND 9.21
Live Deployments:
  • Cloudflare: 1.1.1.1 resolver validates ML-DSA-44 (DNSSEC algorithm 18) DNSSEC signatures by default; dnstest.dev published as a live ML-DSA-44-signed test zone (since 2026-09-10)

chunks.title: Protocol Support Matrix: RPKI / BGPsec
chunks.content:
Protocol: RPKI / BGPsec
Resource Public Key Infrastructure (RPKI certs + ROAs) and BGPsec (per-AS-hop path signatures) — signature-only PKI mechanisms for routing security. RPKI has one very early individual (non-WG) PQC draft; BGPsec has none at all, and itself remains almost entirely undeployed.
PQC Standardization Status:
Pure KEM: na
  Note: RPKI and BGPsec are signature-only PKI mechanisms; no key exchange.
Hybrid KEM: na
  Note: RPKI and BGPsec are signature-only PKI mechanisms; no key exchange.
Pure Signature: experimental
  Note: RPKI certs/ROAs are ordinary X.509 (RFC 5280) + CMS (RFC 6488) objects, so they could technically reuse the generic ML-DSA/SLH-DSA X.509 OIDs (RFC 9881/9909) — but no RPKI-specific draft proposes a pure-PQ profile; the one real draft targets composite only (see Hybrid). The real blocker is repository-scale bulk validation, not the certificate format: every relying party fetches and re-validates the ENTIRE global repository, and a SIDN Labs thesis measured this growing from ~838 MB (RSA-2048) to 3+ GB at ML-DSA-44 and 6.7–14 GB (judged impractical) at SLH-DSA.
Hybrid Signature: draft (individual-draft)
  Stage note: Individual submission (draft-yoshikawa-sidrops-pqc-rpki-01, posted 2026-07-04) — not adopted by the SIDROPS working group, no IESG standing
  Note: Proposes Composite ML-DSA-65 + ECDSA-P256 for RPKI certificates. Explicitly flags open questions: HSM readiness, untested RRDP snapshot/delta size impact, no Krill/relying-party integration yet. BGPsec path signatures have NO PQC work of any kind, chartered or individual — and BGPsec itself remains almost entirely undeployed in production networks (unlike RPKI ROA validation, which covers ~50%+ of routes), which independent sources cite as the reason nobody is prioritizing BGPsec-specific PQC engineering.

Documents: RFC-6480, RFC-8205, RFC-8608, draft-yoshikawa-sidrops-pqc-rpki-02
No live deployments: No RIR (RIPE NCC, ARIN, APNIC) or router vendor (Cisco, Juniper) has announced a PQC-RPKI or PQC-BGPsec pilot. The only PQC-RPKI work anywhere is a single researcher's (SIDN Labs) proof-of-concept patch to Routinator + Krill, published as an MSc thesis — not a production or RIR-run pilot — plus the one five-day-old individual IETF draft above. BGPsec-specific PQC work does not exist at all, consistent with BGPsec's own near-zero real-world deployment despite being standardized since 2017.

chunks.title: Protocol Support Matrix: FIDO 2
chunks.content:
Protocol: FIDO 2
FIDO2 / WebAuthn / passkeys — channel security inherits TLS 1.3; WebAuthn signature algorithms register PQ via COSE.
PQC Standardization Status:
Pure KEM: draft (rfc-editor-queue)
  Stage note: Verified live 2026-09-03: draft-ietf-tls-mlkem-10 (2026-09-02) now shows IESG state 'Approved-announcement sent' — it passed the 2026-09-03 telechat referenced in the prior note (inherited from the TLS 1.3 row).

Hybrid KEM: rfc (rfc-published)
  Note: Inherits TLS 1.3 — X25519MLKEM768 hybrid group, published as RFC 10024 on 2026-08-10.
Pure Signature: experimental (experimental)
  Stage note: RFC 9964 is published, but this cell tracks FIDO adoption rather than the RFC's status: the algorithm IDs are inherited from the COSE row and no FIDO Alliance profile exists. Authenticator-side ML-DSA private keys (~5–7 KB) strain secure-element storage budgets, so 'experimental' is a judgement about deployability, not a stale reading of the datatracker.
  Note: Algorithm IDs sourced from the COSE row. Constraint: authenticator-side ML-DSA private key (~5–7 KB) strains secure-element storage budgets. FIDO's Authenticator Allowed Cryptography List v1.7 (review draft, 2026-05-06) lists ML-KEM and ML-DSA as allowed algorithms, while no FIDO protocol profile for post-quantum authentication exists.
Hybrid Signature: draft (wg-document)

  Note: Composite path inherits from the JOSE row; no FIDO Alliance profile yet.

chunks.title: Protocol Support Matrix: EAP / RADIUS
chunks.content:
Protocol: EAP / RADIUS
Extensible Authentication Protocol (802.1X) + RADIUS AAA transport. TLS-tunneled EAP methods (EAP-TLS/TTLS/PEAP/TEAP) inherit TLS 1.3’s PQC posture; EAP-AKA’ (no TLS tunnel) has its own bespoke ML-KEM work; RadSec inherits TLS/DTLS; legacy RADIUS/UDP has no PQC path at all.
PQC Standardization Status:
Pure KEM: draft (wg-last-call)
  Stage note: EAP-AKA’ bespoke ML-KEM (draft-ietf-emu-pqc-eapaka-02) in WG Last Call — new AT_PUB_KEM/AT_KEM_CT attributes
  Note: TLS-tunneled EAP methods (EAP-TLS/TTLS/PEAP/TEAP) inherit ML-KEM directly from TLS 1.3 (see that row) — no new crypto is defined here, only cert-size/fragmentation mitigation (RFC 9191, draft-ietf-emu-pqc-eap-tls). EAP-AKA’ does not tunnel TLS, so it needs its own KEM carriage: new AT_PUB_KEM / AT_KEM_CT attributes plus attribute-level fragmentation for oversized ML-KEM keys/ciphertexts.
Hybrid KEM: draft (wg-last-call)
  Stage note: EAP-AKA’ bespoke hybrid (draft-ietf-emu-hybrid-pqc-eapaka-01) in WG Last Call — ML-KEM-768 + P-256/X25519 via AT_PUB_HYBRID + HPKE
  Note: TLS-tunneled EAP methods already benefit from TLS 1.3’s X25519MLKEM768 hybrid group in production wherever the underlying TLS stack supports it (see TLS 1.3 row) — no EAP-specific extension needed. EAP-AKA’ defines its own AT_PUB_HYBRID + HPKE construction since it has no TLS layer to inherit from.
Pure Signature: draft (wg-last-call)
  Stage note: wg last call (datatracker 2026-10-15)
  Note: EAP-TLS/TTLS/PEAP/TEAP inherit ML-DSA/SLH-DSA certificates via TLS 1.3 + X.509 (see those rows). The resulting oversized certificate chains are exactly the problem RFC 9191 anticipated (“lattice-based cryptography would have public keys of approximately 1000 bytes and signatures of approximately 2000 bytes”) and draft-ietf-emu-pqc-eap-tls now addresses directly. EAP-AKA’ is a symmetric SIM-credential method with no signature dimension — N/A for that variant.
Hybrid Signature: draft (rfc-editor-queue)
  Note: Same inheritance as Pure Signature — composite ML-DSA certificate chains flow through TLS 1.3 / X.509 (see those rows); EAP-AKA’ is N/A (no signature dimension).

Documents: RFC-2865, RFC-3748, RFC-9048, RFC-9190, RFC-9191, draft-ietf-emu-pqc-eap-tls-02, draft-ietf-emu-pqc-eapaka-02, draft-ietf-emu-hybrid-pqc-eapaka-01, draft-ietf-radext-review-radius-02
No live deployments: No vendor (Cisco ISE, Aruba ClearPass, FreeRADIUS) has announced PQC support for EAP-TLS or RadSec specifically. The one real-world PQC 802.1X measurement is a University of Tübingen research testbed (FreeRADIUS + hostapd, arXiv:2601.22892) — not a shipped product. Legacy RADIUS/UDP (RFC 2865) has no PQC path at all: its MD5-keyed obfuscation is already broken for classical reasons, and draft-ietf-radext-review-radius explicitly states “all new cryptographic work in RADIUS [itself] is forbidden” — the sanctioned exit is full migration to RadSec (TLS/DTLS transport), not an in-place upgrade.

chunks.title: Protocol Support Matrix: PKCS#11
chunks.content:
Protocol: PKCS#11
OASIS PKCS#11 v3.2 — the HSM / crypto-token API, now a full OASIS Standard. v3.2 adds ML-KEM, ML-DSA and SLH-DSA mechanisms (CKM_ML_KEM, CKM_ML_DSA, CKM_SLH_DSA) plus C_EncapsulateKey / C_DecapsulateKey.
PQC Standardization Status:
Pure KEM: rfc (rfc-published)
  Stage note: PKCS#11 v3.2 reached full OASIS Standard 2026-06-03; ML-KEM mechanisms (CKM_ML_KEM)
  Note: ML-KEM-512/768/1024 via CKM_ML_KEM + C_EncapsulateKey / C_DecapsulateKey.
Hybrid KEM: na
  Note: PKCS#11 is a mechanism-level token API; hybrid/composite KEMs are composed by callers, not defined by the spec.
Pure Signature: rfc (rfc-published)
  Stage note: PKCS#11 v3.2 reached full OASIS Standard 2026-06-03; ML-DSA + SLH-DSA mechanisms (CKM_ML_DSA, CKM_SLH_DSA)
  Note: ML-DSA-44/65/87 (incl. HashML-DSA) + SLH-DSA via CKM_ML_DSA / CKM_SLH_DSA.
Hybrid Signature: na
  Note: No native composite-signature mechanism; callers combine atomic per-key signatures above the API.

Documents: PKCS11-v3.2-OS
OSS Libraries: SoftHSM v3 (pqctoday), OpenSSL pkcs11-provider
Live Deployments:
  • pqctoday SoftHSM v3: PKCS#11 v3.2 ML-KEM + ML-DSA software HSM (WASM) — runnable in the in-browser HSM playground (since 2026)
Recommended for production PQC today. PKCS#11 v3.2 (OASIS Standard) specifies ML-KEM and ML-DSA mechanisms, and vendor HSMs implement them. You can try the mechanisms in the HSM playground.

chunks.title: Protocol Support Matrix: KMIP
chunks.content:
Protocol: KMIP
OASIS Key Management Interoperability Protocol v3.0 — key lifecycle over the wire. CSD02 defines ML-KEM and ML-DSA managed-object algorithm enumerations AND the Encapsulate/Decapsulate operations natively; our own server (pqctoday-kmip) implements the full published set — no extensions needed for the PQC KEM/signature core.
PQC Standardization Status:
Pure KEM: draft
  Stage note: OASIS Committee Specification Draft CSD02 (2026-05-07) — ML-KEM algorithm enumerations + native Encapsulate/Decapsulate operations
  Note: ML-KEM-512/768/1024 managed-object algorithm enumerations and the Encapsulate/Decapsulate operations are both defined natively in CSD02 (§6.1.15/§6.1.22, §11.12) — pqctoday-kmip implements the published set directly, no extension needed.
Hybrid KEM: draft
  Stage note: OASIS Committee Specification Draft CSD02 (2026-05-07) — first-class hybrid KEM algorithm values
  Note: X25519MLKEM768 (0x5C) and SecP256r1MLKEM768 (0x5D) are first-class CryptographicAlgorithm values in CSD02 §11.12 — one managed object per hybrid pair, ordinary Encapsulate/Decapsulate, combiner runs inside the engine. Profiles CSD02 §3.3.3 separately mandates a third group, SecP384r1MLKEM1024, as a required TLS key-exchange group for the KMIP transport itself — the Specification still assigns it no managed-object codepoint, so the two documents are currently out of step on that one algorithm.
Pure Signature: draft
  Stage note: OASIS CSD02 (2026-05-07) — ML-DSA algorithm enumeration used by KMIP’s existing Sign / SignatureVerify operations
  Note: ML-DSA-44/65/87 managed objects use the pre-existing KMIP Sign / SignatureVerify operations once the ML-DSA algorithm enum value is present — CSD02 adds the enum (plus 15 pre-hash Hash-ML-DSA-*/Hash-SLH-DSA-* variants, §11.12 Table 552), not new operations.
Hybrid Signature: na
  Note: No native composite-signature object; hybrids are composed above the protocol.

Documents: KMIP-v3.0-CSD02, KMIP-Profiles-v3.0-CSD02
OSS Libraries: pqctoday-kmip
Live Deployments:
  • pqctoday-kmip (CACP): KMIP 3.0 control plane with ML-KEM + ML-DSA and crypto-agility policy — runnable in the in-browser CACP playground (since 2026)

chunks.title: Protocol Support Matrix: Signal (PQXDH)
chunks.content:
Protocol: Signal (PQXDH)
Signal’s post-quantum extended Diffie–Hellman (PQXDH) — the initial key agreement for secure messaging. Hybrid X25519/X448 + ML-KEM (CRYSTALS-Kyber). Deployed in Signal Messenger.
PQC Standardization Status:
Pure KEM: na
  Note: PQXDH is hybrid by construction (classical + PQ KEM); there is no pure-PQ-only mode.
Hybrid KEM: experimental
  Stage note: Signal Foundation specification (Rev 3, 2023; updated 2024-01) — not an IETF/OASIS standard, but live in production
  Note: X25519/X448 ECDH combined with ML-KEM / CRYSTALS-Kyber; mutual auth via classical XEdDSA-signed prekeys.
Pure Signature: na
  Note: PQXDH is key agreement only; prekeys are authenticated with classical XEdDSA, not a PQ signature.
Hybrid Signature: na
  Note: No signature dimension — PQXDH establishes a shared secret.

Documents: Signal-PQXDH-Rev3
OSS Libraries: libsignal
Live Deployments:
  • Signal Messenger: PQXDH (X25519 + ML-KEM/Kyber) as the default initial key agreement for all conversations (since 2023)
  • Signal Messenger (SPQR / Triple Ratchet): Sparse Post-Quantum Ratchet (ML-KEM-768) adds PQ to the continuous ratchet, not just the handshake — rolling out to clients (since 2025-10)

chunks.title: Protocol Support Matrix: Sigstore
chunks.content:
Protocol: Sigstore
Sigstore — keyless software-supply-chain signing (cosign + Fulcio CA + Rekor transparency log). PQC is at the planning stage: the project plan of 2 October 2026 targets a production-ready post-quantum public instance for mid-2027, and the public Fulcio CA still issues classical certificates.
PQC Standardization Status:
Pure KEM: na
  Note: Sigstore is a signing system; no key-encapsulation dimension.
Hybrid KEM: na
  Note: No KEM dimension.
Pure Signature: experimental (identified)
  Stage note: The project has announced an initially opt-in PQC rollout and targets a production-ready PQC public instance for mid-2027
  Note: Sigstore plans a separate, initially opt-in PQC infrastructure. The classical public instance will remain operational and supported while the PQC public instance targets production readiness in mid-2027.
Hybrid Signature: none
  Note: No composite/hybrid signing track in Sigstore yet.
No live deployments: The project targets a production-ready PQC public instance for mid-2027 through an initially opt-in rollout. The classical public instance remains operational and supported during the transition.

chunks.title: Protocol Support Matrix: IEEE 802.11bt (Wi-Fi PQC)
chunks.content:
Protocol: IEEE 802.11bt (Wi-Fi PQC)
IEEE 802.11 amendment adding post-quantum AKM suites, PQC key-establishment/signature algorithms, and a PQC password-authenticated key exchange (PAKE) to the WLAN MAC layer (SAE, OWE, FILS, PASN). Task Group BT has completed Draft 1.0 letter-ballot collection and is preparing Draft 1.1.
PQC Standardization Status:
Pure KEM: draft
  Stage note: PAR approved 2025-09-10 for Task Group BT. Draft 1.0 went to an initial 30-day Working Group Letter Ballot (LB 297); the September 2026 update reports 650 comments received, 232 resolved, and instructions to start Draft 1.1.
  Note: The amendment scope covers PQC AKM suites and PQC key-establishment algorithms across SAE/OWE/FILS/PASN; the public status page does not identify a specific pure KEM construction.
Hybrid KEM: draft
  Stage note: PAR approved 2025-09-10 for Task Group BT. Draft 1.0 went to an initial 30-day Working Group Letter Ballot (LB 297); the September 2026 update reports 650 comments received, 232 resolved, and instructions to start Draft 1.1.
  Note: The amendment scope covers AKM suites and key-establishment algorithms; the public status page does not identify a specific hybrid KEM construction.
Pure Signature: draft
  Stage note: PAR approved 2025-09-10 for Task Group BT. Draft 1.0 went to an initial 30-day Working Group Letter Ballot (LB 297); the September 2026 update reports 650 comments received, 232 resolved, and instructions to start Draft 1.1.
  Note: The amendment scope covers PQC digital signature algorithms and a PQC password-authenticated key exchange (PAKE); the public status page does not identify a specific pure signature scheme.
Hybrid Signature: draft
  Stage note: PAR approved 2025-09-10 for Task Group BT. Draft 1.0 went to an initial 30-day Working Group Letter Ballot (LB 297); the September 2026 update reports 650 comments received, 232 resolved, and instructions to start Draft 1.1.
  Note: The amendment scope covers digital signature algorithms; the public status page does not identify a specific hybrid or composite signature construction.

Documents: IEEE-P802.11bt-PAR
No live deployments: The amendment remains a draft: Draft 1.0 entered Working Group Letter Ballot, and the editor was instructed to begin Draft 1.1 after comment collection.

chunks.title: Protocol Support Matrix: Fibre Channel FC-SP-3
chunks.content:
Protocol: Fibre Channel FC-SP-3
ANSI/INCITS Fibre Channel — Security Protocols, Third Edition. Adds CNSA 2.0 algorithm definitions (ML-KEM, ML-DSA) alongside existing CNSA 1.0 support, plus an automatic in-flight FC encryption profile for SAN fabrics. Completed by the Fibre Channel Industry Association Feb 2026.
PQC Standardization Status:

  Stage note: FC-SP-3 completed Feb 2026 — CNSA 2.0 algorithm definitions added
  Note: FC-SP-3 adds CNSA 2.0 algorithm support (ML-KEM) for FC-SP key exchange. Broadcom Emulex SecureHBA already negotiates ML-KEM-1024 automatically as part of the standard Fibre Channel login process.
Hybrid KEM: na
  Note: FC-SP-3 adopts CNSA 2.0 algorithms directly (pure ML-KEM); no composite/hybrid KEM construct is defined.
Pure Signature: rfc
  Stage note: FC-SP-3 completed Feb 2026 — CNSA 2.0 algorithm definitions added
  Note: FC-SP-3 adds CNSA 2.0 algorithm support (ML-DSA) for FC-SP key/entity authentication. Broadcom Emulex SecureHBA already negotiates ML-DSA-87 automatically as part of the standard Fibre Channel login process.
Hybrid Signature: na
  Note: FC-SP-3 adopts CNSA 2.0 algorithms directly (pure ML-DSA); no composite/hybrid signature construct is defined.

Documents: FC-SP-3
Live Deployments:
  • Broadcom Emulex SecureHBA + Everpure FlashArray//XL130 R5: End-to-end PQC-safe in-flight Fibre Channel encryption — ML-KEM-1024 + ML-DSA-87 key negotiation, AES-GCM-256 data encryption, no measurable performance penalty or CPU overhead (since 2026-03)
Recommended for production PQC today. FC-SP-3 has published CNSA 2.0 (ML-KEM + ML-DSA) algorithm support and a shipping production deployment (Broadcom Emulex SecureHBA, 120,000+ units) with no measured performance cost.

chunks.title: Implementation attack surface: ML-KEM-512 (NIST Level 1)
chunks.content:
Implementation security for: ML-KEM-512 (NIST Level 1)
Known attack vectors: side-channel attacks, fault injection, API misuse
Side-channel attacks: Yes | Fault injection: Yes | RNG failure risk: Unknown
Secret handling failures: Unknown | API misuse risk: Yes
Mitigations: Constant-time decapsulation mandatory (timing leak in NTT/rejection sampling). Validate ciphertext length before processing. Use FIPS 140-3 DRBG for key generation. Zeroize secret key post-use.
IACR reference: https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/2051; https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1577; https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/2009; https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/983

chunks.title: CNSA 2.0 Migration Milestones (NSA)
chunks.content:
CNSA 2.0 — NSA Post-Quantum Cryptography Requirements for National Security Systems
Published: 2022-09-07
2025: New software/firmware should prefer CNSA 2.0 algorithms
2027: New networking equipment must support CNSA 2.0
2030: All deployed NSS software must use CNSA 2.0 signatures exclusively
2031: Legacy networking equipment must be replaced
2031: Full enforcement — all remaining NSS systems (web, cloud, servers)
Scope: National Security Systems (NSS) operated by US government and contractors
Algorithms required: ML-KEM-1024 (KEM), ML-DSA-87 (signatures), SLH-DSA (backup signatures)

chunks.title: NIST Classical Algorithm Deprecation Timeline (IR 8547)
chunks.content:
NIST IR 8547 — Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards
FIPS 203/204/205 finalized: 2024-08-13
2030: Deprecation target for RSA-2048 and 112-bit ECC (NIST SP 800-131A Rev 3)
2035: Full disallowance of classical public-key cryptography

chunks.title: ANSSI PQC Migration Guidance (France)
chunks.content:
ANSSI — French National Cybersecurity Agency PQC Guidance
Hybrid mode mandatory: true — PQC + classical required during transition (except standalone hash-based signatures)
Hash-based signatures standalone allowed: true (SLH-DSA, LMS, XMSS)
Target year for migration plans: undefined
Important: ANSSI and NSA CNSA 2.0 diverge — ANSSI mandates hybrid mode; CNSA 2.0 allows pure PQC for NSS at GA.
Source: ANSSI "Avis relatif à la migration vers la cryptographie post-quantique" (2024 / r3 2025)

chunks.title: BSI PQC Recommendations (Germany)
chunks.content:
BSI TR-02102 — German Federal Office for Information Security
Hybrid PQC + classical recommended during transition: true
Target for quantum-safe by default: 2030
Source: BSI TR-02102 Cryptographic Mechanisms: Recommendations and Key Lengths (2024)

chunks.title: CRQC Arrival Estimates (Research Consensus)
chunks.content:
CRQC (Cryptographically Relevant Quantum Computer) Arrival — Research Consensus Estimates
Conservative lower bound: 2030
Moderate estimate: 2035
Upper bound: 2040
"Harvest now, decrypt later" attacks mean data encrypted today with classical crypto is at risk even before CRQC arrival.
Implication: PQC migration urgency is independent of exact CRQC timeline — long-lived sensitive data needs protection now.

chunks.title: Cross-agency disagreement: Hybrid PQC + classical KEM is the recommended deployment pat
chunks.content:
Counter-claim / Cross-agency disagreement (cc-001)
Record: CNSA-2 (compliance)
Competing source: anssi-pqc-roadmap
Position in dispute: "Hybrid PQC + classical KEM is the recommended deployment pattern for the transition window"
Disagreement: NSA CNSA 2.0 §2.1 mandates ML-KEM as the sole approved KEM for NSS at GA; ANSSI's "guide pour la transition vers la cryptographie post-quantique" (Jan 2024 / r3 2025) recommends hybrid (ECDHE + ML-KEM) deployments through at least 2030 for systems handling sensitive (DR) data. Both are Tier-1 government sources giving operationally divergent guidance for systems that must comply with both regimes.
Verified by: ericamador on 2026-05-08
